title: Architecture gaps and agent change plan
text: HIVE — Architecture Gap Audit and Agent Change Plan Document type: Implementation handoff / agent change specification Prepared: 2026-11-20 Target: HIVE architecture, research vault, experiment system, learning infrastructure, and public HIVE documentation Entry point: https://mominc.online/hive/ Status: Proposed changes — verify against the actual repository and local environment before editing. --- 0. Instructions to the Implementing Agent You are tasked with turning HIVE from a primarily research- and architecture-driven project into a measurable, incrementally self-improving modular AI system. Preserve useful existing work; do not perform an indiscriminate rewrite. Your first actions: 1. Inspect the actual source repository, project structure, running services, available models/tools, local documentation vault, test suite, and deployed HIVE website. Do not assume public website pages reflect the full implementation. 2. Map this document's requirements to real modules and files. Where paths are unknown, discover them rather than inventing them. 3. Identify what already exists, what is partially implemented, and what is missing. Produce a short CURRENT_STATE.md with evidence: file paths, tests, commands, and observed behavior. 4. Propose the smallest safe implementation sequence that creates an end-to-end validated learning cycle. Execute within granted permissions; for destructive or production-impacting changes, request approval. 5. Preserve existing research, links, alternative hypotheses, and experiment history. Prefer additive, reversible migrations with compatibility checks. 6. Record all decisions, changes, test commands, benchmark artifacts, failures, and blockers in an agent change log. Do not report a feature as implemented until exercised by a reproducible test. Critical constraints: - Do not claim that planned architecture is implemented, or that archived simulation results validate full-scale real-model operation. - Do not autonomously deploy experimental neural weights, routing policies, changed permissions, or high-impact code changes into production. - Do not train on hidden evaluation examples or allow the candidate's evaluator to rewrite success criteria. - Do not optimize only for a single combined score. Enforce authorization, correctness, safety, and resource limits as independent gates. - Do not delete research branches that disagree. Mark their evidence and status instead. - Prioritize operating on the user's existing local software and hardware where verified available; avoid adding infrastructure merely for architectural elegance. --- 1. Executive Decision Problem HIVE has a strong body of research on specialist systems, protected memories, adaptive routing, verification, organizational alternatives, and sleep-inspired consolidation. Its key deficiency is the lack of a verified, integrated system that demonstrably improves future performance by learning from previous work. The site describes architecture and experiments, but documentation explicitly distinguishes plans from implementation. Historic small NumPy simulations and scheduling experiments are useful preliminary evidence, not substitutes for reproducible real-model benchmarks. Recommended change Make an Empirical Learning Engine the central development priority. It should collect episodes, evaluate outcomes, assign credit, propose limited changes, test them against unchanged baselines, and promote changes only through controlled gates. Shift in development logic: - Current emphasis: Research → Architecture → Build → Learning - Proposed emphasis: Measure → Build → Learn → Test → Adapt → Measure again First milestone: A complete task → execution → independent evaluation → failure diagnosis → candidate improvement → held-out evaluation → promotion/rollback cycle, demonstrated on an actual local workflow. --- 2. What to Preserve Do not replace the following simply because this plan modifies the priority order: 1. Modular, specialized AI and deterministic software components. 2. Independent verification and evidence-based conclusions. 3. Explicit separation of research, source code, execution, and model/adapter artifacts. 4. Multiple candidate organizational designs that can compete experimentally. 5. Segmented memory, provenance, replay, and regression awareness. 6. Human- or policy-controlled permissions, deployment, and high-consequence decisions. 7. The existing research graph and historical reasoning, including disagreements and failed experiments. 8. Reusable software adapters; a calculator, parser, database query, or media probe should be preferred over an LLM where it is more accurate and efficient. --- 3. Priority Gap Register A gap below means no publicly demonstrated end-to-end mechanism or insufficiently specified behavior in the reviewed documentation. Verify the code before marking it absent. ID Priority Gap Required agent change Proof of completion --------------- G01 P0 No proven end-to-end learning loop Create a bounded episode-to-improvement pipeline A failed example results in a candidate correction that improves held-out performance or is rejected with evidence G02 P0 Governing formulas uncalibrated Implement configurable, logged decision functions with measured inputs Reproduce routing decisions from stored evidence and configuration G03 P0 No unified real-model/tool benchmark record Build a benchmark runner and capability registry Results include task, configuration, accuracy, latency, resource use, and artifacts G04 P0 Compounding learning not demonstrated Benchmark learning efficiency across successive task distributions Learning curves include uncertainty and compare against unchanged controls G05 P1 Credit assignment not operationally validated Compare components through ablations/counterfactual tests Identified improvements persist when the purported contributor is used and disappear or diminish in a suitable control G06 P1 Adaptive organization not learned from results Begin fixed, then train a contextual router Router beats a static policy on held-out workload without breaking constraints G07 P1 Feedback-to-training pipeline not demonstrated Create an event store and curated dataset builder Provenance-aware validated examples are exportable and auditable G08 P1 Research graph confused with runtime capability graph Introduce a separate operational capability/dependency registry Each operational component exposes executable contract, health, restrictions, and evidence G09 P1 Hardware scheduling not empirically optimized Track actual load, VRAM/RAM use, startup cost, latency, and queueing Scheduler makes reproducible, budget-constrained decisions G10 P1 Memory correction/expiry lacks integrated proof Add provenance, invalidation, correction, isolated partitions, retrieval tests Contradictory or stale memories are flagged, do not silently overwrite truth, and can be rolled back G11 P1 Checker reliability not calibrated Track verifier false acceptance, false rejection, and verification cost Calibration curves and comparison against independent labels G12 P2 Broad research may not resolve build decisions Prioritize research by expected experimental impact Research queue links hypothesis → deciding experiment → decision record Explicit unknowns - The public site's stated research-page counts and other counters are documentation metadata, not implementation KPIs. - Historical references to approximately 360 NumPy learning runs and 1,440 scheduling simulations are archival claims; inspect original artifacts before relying on them. - The local repository, hardware configuration, model readiness, and available tests have not been independently inspected by this handoff. Inventory before choosing components or committing to performance targets. --- 4. Target Architecture mermaid flowchart TD A[Goals, observations, tasks, constraints] -- B[Eligibility & adaptive decision engine] B -- C[AI specialists] B -- D[Deterministic software experts] B -- E[Bounded supervisors] C -- F[Evidence & independent verification] D -- F E -- F F -- G[Episode and experience store] G -- H[Empirical learning engine] H -- I[Credit assignment & failure analysis] I -- J[Candidate procedures, router policies, memories, adapters] J -- K[Isolated sandbox & held-out evaluation] K -- L{Promotion gates passed?} L -- No -- M[Reject / diagnose / archive] L -- Yes -- N[Versioned release with rollback] N -- B N -- C N -- D N -- E Architectural boundaries - Task/goal layer: Defines inputs, success criteria, constraints, permissions, and budget. - Adaptive decision engine: Selects authorized configurations; may use a deterministic policy before a learned one. - Specialist execution: Invokes interchangeable models, adapters, tools, and monitors with observable contracts. - Independent verification: Uses rule-based checks, independent models where justified, ground-truth comparisons, or human judgments. A checker must not be assumed accurate merely because it is a second model. - Experience store: Captures complete evidence/provenance without mixing raw observations with approved reusable knowledge. - Learning engine: Proposes updates to procedures first, then routing/memory, then model weights when supported by evidence. - Promotion governor: Applies immutable approval and regression criteria; promotion is separate from proposal generation. Separation-of-duties rule: An experimental agent cannot both modify its acceptance gates and approve deployment of its own changes. --- 5. Five Governing Deciders to Implement Implement these as separate, composable policies. Record all inputs, assumptions, policy versions, scores, and rejection reasons. Avoid treating their initial mathematical forms as proven or universally optimal. D1 — Eligibility (hard gate) Construct the feasible action set: \[ F(x) = \{a : \text{authorized}(a,x) \land \text{compatible}(a,x) \land \text{withinBudget}(a,x) \land \text{safe}(a,x)\} \] This is not a weighted preference: an option violating a hard constraint must be ineligible regardless of estimated quality. D2 — Task-conditioned routing \[ a^ = \arg\max_{a\in F(x)} [\hat p(a\mid x)V(x) - \lambda_C C(a,x) - \lambda_T T(a,x) - \lambda_R R(a,x)] \] Variables: - x: task context and constraints. - a: configuration (models + tools + workflow + checker depth). - p_hat: calibrated estimate of verified task success, conditional on context. - V: measured or defined value of success. - C: projected compute/resource cost. - T: projected latency. - R: measurable residual risk after mandatory safeguards. - lambda_: task-context-specific trade-offs; determine through experiments, not arbitrary permanent constants. Initial policy: use constrained, transparent heuristics; record counterfactual alternatives. Train a contextual selector only after enough quality-controlled examples exist. D3 — Verification value Request another check only when its expected improvement in decision quality exceeds its additional cost, subject to compulsory checks. \[ \operatorname{EVI}(v\mid x) = \mathbb E[U\mid\text{result of }v,x] - U(\text{current decision}\mid x) - C(v) \] Keep mandatory verification regardless of calculated EVI. Compare whether extra checks improve outcomes or simply add latency/false alarms. D4 — Learning / experiment priority \[ \operatorname{EV}(e) = \frac{P(\text{valid improvement}\mid e)\cdot \mathbb E[\Delta Q_{\text{future}}\mid e] - \text{cost}(e) - \text{risk}(e)}{\text{scarce resource usage}(e)} \] Treat this as a candidate ranking heuristic, not an objectively known quantity. Estimate uncertainty and prioritize experiments that could change an upcoming decision. Retain low-confidence competing hypotheses for testing. D5 — Promotion / release gate A candidate can advance only if all required conditions pass: - Held-out quality improves enough to matter or achieves an independently specified cost reduction without meaningful quality loss. - No unacceptable regression on safety, prior capabilities, memory integrity, or required tasks. - Resource and latency budgets remain within limits. - Evidence and artifacts are reproducible, including versions and seeds where possible. - The approving policy/human has authority to promote this class of change. - A rollback path is available and tested. Prefer confidence intervals, repeated trials, and practical effect sizes to a single pass/fail score. Track variance across tasks and seeds. Learning-speed indicator For a predefined fixed performance threshold: \[ G_{\text{learn}} = 1 - \frac{N_{\text{HIVE}}}{N_{\text{baseline}}} \] N is the number of examples or trials needed to reach that threshold. A positive value indicates improved sample efficiency, not necessarily superior final capability. Separately measure total compute, wall time, generalization, retention, and catastrophic forgetting. --- 6. Data and Interface Requirements Do not introduce a major database solely because a graph seems useful. Use the simplest viable durable implementation; make the schema portable. Required records Record Required fields ------ TaskSpec task_id, task_type, input_ref, success_criteria_version, permissions, resource_budget, split_id, created_at Capability capability_id, kind, version, endpoint/adapter, supported_tasks, constraints, health, provenance Config config_id, component_versions, routing_policy_version, tool_graph, checker_policy_version, limits Episode episode_id, task_id, config_id, input_hash, trace_refs, output_refs, timings, resources, status, errors Verification episode_id, checker_id, checker_version, criteria_version, result, confidence_if_calibrated, evidence_refs, label_source FailurePattern pattern_id, episode_refs, hypothesis, severity, provenance, status ChangeCandidate candidate_id, parent_version, change_type, diff_or_artifact_ref, hypothesis, training_data_refs, scope Experiment experiment_id, candidate_id, control_config_id, task_split_versions, metrics, seed, result_artifacts, decision Release release_id, candidate_id, approval_ref, gate_results, deployed_version, rollback_ref, timestamp MemoryItem memory_id, partition, content_ref, source_refs, confidence, validation_status, created_at, expires_at, supersedes, access_policy Implementation essentials - Every task execution produces an append-only, inspectable episode/event trace; sensitive payloads require appropriate redaction or protected storage. - Keep raw_observations, inferred_claims, validated_facts, and deployable_procedures separate. - Prevent train/test contamination using versioned splits, data lineage, and immutable holdouts. - Version policy definitions and rubric definitions separately from specialist weights and procedures. - Store component compatibility, resource requirements, dependencies, and health in the operational capability registry. - Maintain cross-links to the existing research graph, but do not make research pages executable authorities. - Add clean, replaceable adapters so services can be swapped without rewriting the controller. --- 7. Change the Build Order Phase 0 — Reconnaissance and baseline (required) Tasks: 1. Inventory actual repository/files, model availability, services, tests, runtime endpoints, GPU/CPU/RAM/VRAM, and current vault structure. 2. Locate existing experiment artifacts; identify which can actually be rerun. 3. Map existing functionality against G01–G12 and classify each implemented / partial / planned / unsupported. 4. Select a first target workflow with deterministic checks and non-destructive outputs. 5. Run a fixed baseline and save raw outcomes and reproducible commands. Deliverables: CURRENT_STATE.md, CAPABILITY_INVENTORY.md, BASELINE_RESULTS.md, and machine-readable run artifacts. Exit gate: At least one real workflow, one runnable baseline, and documented independent success criteria. Phase 1 — Minimum empirical organism (P0) Tasks: 1. Implement task specs, capability registration, execution traces, resource telemetry, and independent checkers. 2. Create a simple constrained router with explicit tool/model compatibility and budget gates. 3. Add an event store with provenance and repeatable test fixtures. 4. Implement one complete deterministic/LLM-assisted workflow with graceful timeouts and failure recording. 5. Add a replayable benchmark runner with control configurations. Exit gate: Run the same task set across at least three configurations; produce comparable quality, cost, latency, and failure metrics without hand-entered results. Phase 2 — First verified learning cycle (P0) Tasks: 1. Find a repeated failure in the task outcomes. 2. Generate a bounded procedure-level change (for example, a tool invocation rule, validated template, recovery path, or checker addition). 3. Evaluate the candidate on development tasks, then frozen held-out tasks. 4. Compare against the unchanged control and detect regressions. 5. Pass through explicit promotion approval and versioning; verify rollback. 6. Measure whether similar future tasks require fewer corrections/trials. Exit gate: The complete cycle is automated except for any defined approval boundary, and an accepted or rejected candidate has fully inspectable evidence. Accepted candidates must show meaningful held-out benefit. Rejection is a valid scientific outcome but not evidence of learning improvement. Phase 3 — Learn organizational choices (P1) Tasks: 1. Evaluate static routing versus data-conditioned routing under identical resource limits. 2. Compare one specialist, multiple independent specialists, and structured specialist/tool groups. 3. Run ablations: remove one expert/checker/tool at a time and measure actual contribution. 4. Add optional contextual bandit/learned router with exploration bounds and off-policy evaluation where appropriate. 5. Train and test specialist-selection policies on genuinely different task conditions; guard against overfitting. Exit gate: Learned organization yields reproducible held-out improvements over the best simple baseline, not merely over a deliberately weak comparator. Phase 4 — Specialist and memory learning (P1/P2) Tasks: 1. Compare retrieval, reusable procedures, and adapter fine-tuning before modifying core model weights. 2. Test isolated training, shared adapters, replay, distillation, pruning, and checkpoint swapping where technically feasible. 3. Measure interference, forgetting, startup cost, and deployment overhead. 4. Introduce sleep-inspired consolidation only as a testable job type (deduplication, memory replay, model update evaluation), not a biological metaphor without a mechanism. 5. Keep all model updates inside immutable checkpoints with separated staging and production. Exit gate: A justified learning method improves capability or efficiency while passing retention, provenance, privacy, and rollback tests. --- 8. First Experiment: Video Production Workflow This is the recommended initial experiment, not a claim that all required software is currently working. Validate local readiness first. Candidate tasks - Inspect media and extract reliable metadata. - Validate captions/subtitle timing or formatting against reference checks. - Propose edit segments and produce non-destructive cut lists/EDLs. - Produce draft title/description options under defined constraints. - Validate output formats and run a dry-run publishing queue (no autonomous posting). Pilot design - Development set: 40–60 representative tasks. - Frozen held-out set: 20–30 representative tasks. - Initial configurations: 3 (deterministic tools alone; one model + the same tools; specialist-assisted combination). - First learner update: one bounded reusable procedure. - Include easy, difficult, and adversarial/edge-case tasks; stratify the held-out split by source and task type. - Treat proposed sample sizes as a pilot starting point, not a statistically validated power calculation. Scorecard Report at least: 1. Verified success and error categories by task type. 2. Quality of independent checker against ground truth or human reference labels. 3. End-to-end latency and startup/load latency. 4. VRAM/RAM/CPU utilization and resource-time cost. 5. Model/tool calls, retries, and human interventions. 6. Retention on previously solved tasks. 7. Improvement on frozen held-out tasks after the correction. 8. Confidence intervals or uncertainty estimates where justified. 9. Transfer performance on a related but unseen task family when feasible. Comparison rule: Keep task definitions, checker criteria, and budgets consistent across configurations; record where deterministic-only approaches are inapplicable rather than penalizing them unfairly. Follow-on evaluation: After the pilot demonstrates a repeatable learning loop, test transfer to the live streaming supervisor and horror game workflows. Do not prematurely optimize all three at once. --- 9. Website / Vault Changes Goal: Make the public HIVE website distinguish research, specification, implementation, and experimental evidence at a glance. Add or expose the following views View Purpose Minimum content --------- Implementation Status Show what runs today Components, readiness, links to tests/artifacts, last verified date Experiment Registry Make studies reproducible Hypothesis, controls, task splits, metric definitions, results, artifacts, status Capability Registry Describe executable components Models, software adapters, supported tasks, resource profiles, health, versions Learning Progress Show whether HIVE compounds Baselines vs updated variants, sample efficiency, quality, cost, retention, uncertainty Decision Ledger Preserve competing designs and why choices were made Alternatives, evidence, decision, reviewer, confidence, reevaluation trigger Known Gaps Keep important unknowns visible Gap owner, experiment needed, status, dependencies, evidence Change / Release History Make improvement traceable Candidate, tested diff, gates, approvals, release, rollback Documentation conventions - Add a status marker to research statements: HYPOTHESIS, SPECIFIED, IMPLEMENTED, MEASURED, REPLICATED, or REJECTED (a research claim may have multiple dimensions; keep definitions precise). - Distinguish archival simulations from live-model benchmarks. - Hyperlink hypothesis → proposed mechanism → code/tests → runs → results → decision. - Preserve existing pages and outgoing links; avoid replacing long-form research with a dashboard. - Do not publish credentials, private user content, local endpoints, proprietary files, or raw sensitive traces. - Clearly label stale results and latest verified dates. Relevant public pages to cross-reference - HIVE home - Framework - Roadmap - Adaptive Research - History / previous experiments - Runtime contracts - Benchmark plan Do not infer filesystem paths from URLs. Locate the actual source files during Phase 0. --- 10. Tests and Acceptance Criteria Tests to implement - Routing eligibility: Unauthorized, incompatible, unavailable, or over-budget actions must never be selected. - Tool failure: Missing service, malformed output, timeout, and resource exhaustion trigger bounded recovery or explicit failure—not infinite retry loops. - Trace completeness: Each run is attributable to exact task and config versions, with verifiable output references. - Reproducibility: Same frozen task set and config can be rerun; nondeterminism and seed variation are explicitly represented. - Independent evaluation: The component being improved cannot control hidden test outcomes or modify frozen acceptance rubrics. - Contamination prevention: Training examples and test cases are versioned and separated; leakage checks are part of evaluation. - Regression: Prior tasks, tool compatibility, permissions, and budget adherence are evaluated before promotion. - Rollback: Previous known-good configuration can be restored after a simulated bad release. - Memory safety: Corrections/supersession are logged; contradictory claims are not silently merged; expired entries are not treated as current truth. - Scalability: Track concurrent requests and contention empirically before scaling from a handful of components to hundreds. Minimum Definition of Done for first release - [ ] Real local capability inventory checked and documented. - [ ] At least one non-destructive task family executes end-to-end. - [ ] Three baseline configurations can be benchmarked, or exclusions are technically justified. - [ ] Structured episode, verifier, candidate, experiment, and release records exist. - [ ] A candidate improvement can be generated from observed failure evidence. - [ ] Held-out comparison and regression gates run without changing scoring rules. - [ ] Candidate can be accepted or rejected with inspectable evidence. - [ ] Versioning and rollback are proven in a test. - [ ] At least one documented improvement in held-out performance exists before any compounding learning achieved claim is made. - [ ] Public documentation accurately separates plans, partial builds, and demonstrated operation. --- 11. What Not to Build First Unless specific experiments justify them, defer: - Hundreds or thousands of active agents/models. - A sophisticated learned master controller trained before quality data exists. - A new graph database or bespoke inter-agent language as a prerequisite for baseline experiments. - Unbounded autonomous weight rewrites or production hot-swapping. - Infrastructure that cannot be tied to a measurable failure or bottleneck. - Full real-time streaming/game automation before success on a reproducible non-destructive workload. Preserve these as research hypotheses and alternatives; do not delete or dismiss them without testing. --- 12. Handoff Output Expected from the Implementing Agent Provide these in the repository or designated HIVE workspace, adapting names to existing conventions: text CURRENT_STATE.md Grounded audit of repository and services CAPABILITY_INVENTORY.md Real model/tool availability and readiness GAP_IMPLEMENTATION_MAP.md G01-G12 mapped to files, owners, and statuses ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md Choices and trade-offs, including rejected options EXPERIMENT_REGISTRY. Machine-readable experiment manifests/results BASELINE_RESULTS.md First real benchmark with evidence links LEARNING_LOOP_REPORT.md First candidate, test, decision, and rollback proof CHANGELOG.md Modified files and test commands For every delivered change, report: - What changed (specific file paths and behavior). - What was already implemented and therefore left intact. - What was measured (metrics and raw artifacts). - What failed or remains unknown (do not fabricate results). - Which gates passed and any blocked releases. - Next smallest experiment that will reduce uncertainty. Final instruction Optimize for evidence of compounding learning, not architectural complexity. The first proof of progress is that HIVE can use experience to improve its future work in a measured, reproducible, resource-aware way—without losing prior capabilities or silently promoting bad changes.

title: Autonomous local prototype — v0.1
text: Autonomous local prototype — v0.1 IMPLEMENTED / MEASURED. Learned candidate QUARANTINED. HIVE now has a local Python/SQLite executor that calls a real local model, verifies its outputs, retains evidence across restarts, and changes routing from development feedback. This is a separate experiment from the earlier caption pilot. It demonstrates policy adaptation within a small synthetic suite, not general superiority or model-weight training. The public website remains a static record. Last verified: 21 November 2026 UTC (20 November locally). Source commit: 9c6c33170d0d94bb0aecbbadc2842ad7731136de in the local HIVE repo. The publication manifest binds the exported files and download to that commit. What runs - A task declares measurable success criteria before execution. The CLI selects a model/tool route, records requests, outputs and resource usage, and checks the result with an independent deterministic verifier. - A durable SQLite queue retains ownership, history, feedback and checkpoints. A real failed development task automatically queued a successful tool follow-up. Process-crash recovery, stop/resume, stale-owner rejection and rollback are tested. - Fixed, random, greedy and UCB policies are compared. Beta reliability and cost-aware utility update only from valid development observations. Alternative objectives and prior sensitivity are descriptive diagnostics. - The candidate freezes before validation. Holdout IDs are consumed before dispatch; validation and holdout outputs never update the policy. Promotion requires trusted independent evidence review. No real candidate was promoted. Recorded experiment One real Ollama model: myr5-hold-local:latest, Qwen 9B Q4_K_M, on an RTX 5070 Ti. Exact model digest: a45646773d1ee8a6c1557c7de09a68e78a74f2990c4174a1408f65e777db150c. The preregistered matrix contains 18 development, 12 validation and 24 held-out tasks, six synthetic families, three routes, 108 model calls and 162 observations. The policies below replay shared outcomes; they are not separate online deployments. Policy Held-out verified passes ------: Fixed direct model 12/24 Learning disabled 12/24 Seeded random 16/24 Greedy 23/24 UCB 23/24 Deterministic tools 24/24 Fixed model-plus-tool team 24/24 The UCB-minus-direct quality difference is 0.4583; the descriptive paired 95% bootstrap interval is [0.25, 0.6667]. The rows share six family templates, so this interval cannot establish broad statistical superiority. Greedy ties UCB; deterministic tools outperform both. The learning-disabled comparison supports a within-suite contribution from learned routing, not an advantage over the best tool. The campaign generated 3,725 tokens. Selected UCB outcomes used 586 tokens and 7.657 seconds, versus 1,053 tokens and 11.784 seconds for fixed direct, with 24 model calls each. Tool-only used no model tokens; its near-zero recorded latency is below clock resolution, not physically zero compute cost. Equal per-call caps do not imply equal realized cost. Validation and per-category aggregates are in the full comparison. Verification and decision 52 pytest tests passed, plus the tools-only CLI end-to-end journey and a clean Git-archive task/review/status check. All 162 saved outputs reverified in a fresh process. A separate six-case fresh-inference check matched all six original verified scores with an unchanged policy. These are different reproduction checks. Grok supplied adversarial code review and an independent experiment review; the configured NVIDIA Nemotron reviewer supplied mathematical critique. Recommendations were assessed against evidence, not treated as proof. Review findings produced fail-closed and recovery regression tests. The experiment review recommends QUARANTINE. Its packet preceded the later six-case inference check; that pass does not resolve the stronger-baseline or correlated-template limits. Positive promotion and regression rollback are exercised with explicitly synthetic test approvals. They do not authorize a real policy release. Website publication publishes source and evidence; it does not install the experimental policy. Source, evidence and reproduction - Complete source ZIP - Run instructions - Build and experiment log - Review findings and dispositions - Six fresh-inference checks - Final governance decision - Next experiments Extract the ZIP and follow its README. Python 3.11+ runs the core without runtime dependencies; pytest is needed for tests. Real inference requires local Ollama and the installed model. Nothing downloads a model automatically. The ZIP exports committed source and public evidence only: private evaluator stores, holdout labels and per-case holdout outputs are excluded. A new local campaign creates new evidence; it cannot reconstruct the original private holdout artifacts from public aggregates. Limits and next action The build used 118 of its 120 local-model requests, including probes and the six fresh checks. Workers are stopped. A full new comparison exceeds the remaining two requests. Next: preregister independent task families and a fresh holdout, including an incorrect-tool control, under a new bounded mission. The code-repair evaluator uses finite patch fixtures, not arbitrary repository editing. Memory learning, workflow learning and verifier calibration remain separate queued experiments. No weights were trained. Application budgets do not enforce OS CPU/GPU quotas on Ollama. Holdout separation is a trusted-local logical boundary, not protection against the filesystem owner. Repeated improvement across independent experiments remains unproven. Ongoing publication Ian requested live repository updates as completed work and experiments progress. Each verified milestone will publish its source revision, evidence, failures, decision, limitations and next action here. Publishing a report does not promote a candidate, replenish an inference budget or imply a worker is still running.

title: Adaptive verified controller — v0.2
text: Adaptive verified controller — v0.2 Current executable: v0.2.1 The post-review runtime passed 136 tests, with one Windows symlink test skipped, and both Tester Army CLI journeys. It fixes persistent request/token pause reasons, immediately blocks model identity drift, holds ownership through cleanup, isolates experimental feedback even after process death, and records wall usage atomically. Grok identified these edge cases; the targeted regressions now pass. NVIDIA's statistics critique also removed utility-only acceptance. Download current executable source and evidence · Current source manifest · Current controller source · Final test results · Grok review and dispositions Measurement provenance: the real 30-call run below executed v0.2.0. Its original executable snapshot is preserved separately. The later review fixes used synthetic tests and spent no further model calls. Changing source cannot silently resume an older experiment store. Preserved v0.2.0 experiment and executable Download executable source and public evidence · Publication manifest · Real run · Fresh-process verification · Tests · Controller source Last verified: 21 November 2026 UTC. Executable runtime commit 3d5522ae60735f3c7ffb2b754022c2ae3a328436. The adaptive CLI now constructs a frozen router from verified development feedback, tests it, verifies paired results, diagnoses rejection, retains or replaces an experimental checkpoint, and continues through bounded alternatives. This changes routing policy, not model weights or arbitrary repository code. Executed local run Run d8a941b2f587 used real Ollama inference with myr5-hold-local:latest, Qwen 9B Q4_K_M. Model manifest: a45646773d1ee8a6c1557c7de09a68e78a74f2990c4174a1408f65e777db150c. Twelve development observations trained the frozen router. The same six separate validation tasks were then executed for each candidate and baseline. Route Verified passes Decision ------:--- Direct local model baseline 3/6 Initial experimental incumbent Learned greedy router 5/6 Accepted experimentally; two wins, zero losses Fixed model-plus-tool 4/6 Rejected for a critical regression; retained learned router Deterministic tools 6/6 Continued after rejection; accepted experimentally Thirty model calls, 36 observations, 1,013 generated tokens, 3,840 reserved tokens, 23.451 active execution seconds. Mission caps were 48 requests, 6,144 reserved tokens, 900 active seconds, 100 cycles, 64 MiB artifacts and one local inference. The completed run has 18 unspent requests; the controller does not reset budgets or launch an unbounded daemon. Approved checkpoint remains null. The report is experiments/results/adaptive-real-model.json; fresh-process verification is experiments/results/adaptive-fresh-process-verification.json. All 36 saved observations and candidate decisions reverified with zero new model calls. The private SQLite store remains under .hive/adaptive-v02-20261121. Tests and defects resolved 122 runtime tests passed. Two Tester Army tools-only CLI journeys passed, including STOP → resume → completed replay without spending more budget. The exporter passed 10 tests; one filesystem symlink test was skipped because Windows did not permit creating the test symlink. The initial STOP CLI failure is retained in experiments/results/adaptive-e2e-initial-failure.json. Fixed defects include ordinary STOP returning an error, wrong-job evidence substitution, unchecked cached evidence on partial resume, and a process-death window splitting an incumbent change from its decision. Decisions now commit atomically and reproduce from verified evidence on resume. Tests inject death at that write boundary, test a real child-process exit, corrupt evidence, alter plans and exhaust budgets. Research and limits Sol implemented paired descriptive assessment; Luna implemented the controller; Terra tested recovery and adversarial cases. NVIDIA Nemotron reviewed the statistical plan. Its useful challenge removed utility-only acceptance: quality must improve strictly without critical regression. Utility and family dispersion are descriptive. The NVIDIA review and dispositions are saved with the results. Repeated validation is candidate-selection evidence, not an unused holdout. Six correlated synthetic families and one model cannot demonstrate generalization, compounding learning, weight training or superiority over the strongest simple baseline. Deterministic tools won this run. Their measured zero latency is below timer resolution, not zero physical compute. A candidate's acceptance is only experimental; it cannot approve its own production checkpoint. The next research bottleneck is a preregistered suite with unseen families and tasks on which neither simple route saturates. Repeated inference and negative controls must precede any broad gain claim. Model output still cannot execute arbitrary code, change evaluators, or expand resource limits. Execute powershell $env:PYTHONPATH = "$PWD\src" python -m hive --store .hive/new-adaptive adaptive --config configs/adaptive.json --rounds 3 --output experiments/results/new-adaptive.json python scripts/verify_adaptive.py --store .hive/new-adaptive --config configs/adaptive.json --output experiments/results/new-verification.json A new store spends a new budget; the example is not an instruction to run repeatedly without an aggregate limit. Restart the identical adaptive command with its original store, source and configuration to resume an interrupted run.

title: v0.3 foundation and next experiment
text: HIVE v0.3 foundation — 21 November 2026 Experimental engineering checkpoint; E0 completed with a recorded status defect, E1 draft, no policy deployed. Working branch: build/v0.3, based on published v0.2.1 commit eeec51497038ec34454d867f55ebe0fcadfffddf. This additive source is version 0.3.0.dev1; it is not the source of the older v0.2.0 real-model measurements. Final foundation checks: 217 tests passed, one skipped, plus both Tester Army CLI journeys. The initial full run found only an outdated exporter fixture count after adding plans to the snapshot; the corrected assertion and passing rerun are retained. Reports: experiments/results/v03-foundation-tests.xml and experiments/results/v03-foundation-e2e/report.json. Reproduced release base The live v0.2.1 publication manifest and downloaded ZIP match: - ZIP SHA-256: cd0c782e476f52c75952c923abc5cf16ca6dcbcd3a188c6f4f3c60102f03c445. - Runtime source SHA-256: 2f1ad5f919ec8918a6d699ee0c4328438e5b203294e4048717c0134c9e9bc37f. - Local model digest: a45646773d1ee8a6c1557c7de09a68e78a74f2990c4174a1408f65e777db150c. - Baseline verification: 136 tests passed, one Windows symlink test skipped; both existing Tester Army CLI journeys passed. No new inference was used. experiments/results/v03-base-verification.json records the downloaded payload checks and doctor output. The original ZIP is retained locally under .hive/v03-base/; the historical public artifacts are unchanged. An additional check of the extracted pinned download passed 136 tests with one skip; experiments/results/v03-base-tests-confirmation.xml records that run. Executable addition hive.benchmark_registry.BenchmarkRegistry stores frozen manifests and exposure records in SQLite. It validates source genealogy metadata, binds each fixture's hash to canonical public JSON, rejects cross-split and cross-manifest identity or fixture reuse, and removes private labels from public envelopes. Holdout/future exposure commits atomically before returning data. An exact mission/policy/ evaluator/manifest identity can resume; it is marked reused, never fresh. Terra's independent tests found and reproduced three reuse defects in the first implementation: identical fixture across splits under new IDs, consumed cases copied into a second manifest, and identical held-out fixtures relabeled within the same split. Luna repaired them; the counterexamples remain tests. Astra found and fixed a fourth case: identical public payloads counted twice under distinct sources in one manifest. Duplicate fixture content now fails within the manifest too. Terra's stable recovery/integrity run passed 27 tests, including ten new controls. This is a logical boundary for a trusted curator/process. It cannot authenticate the semantic independence of sources, prevent answers disguised inside text, protect against the OS owner, or make arbitrary generated code safe. Registry identity strings must be bound to actual policy/config/evaluator hashes by the future campaign adapter. The old adaptive runner does not yet use this registry. Its public envelope contains metadata; only nested public is intended for future candidate requests. No independent benchmark corpus or evaluator service has been completed or consumed. Grok independently reproduced numeric/Unicode fixture aliases, disguised answer keys, invisible identifiers and tuple coercion. The repairs preserve the wire fixture hash, add a separate normalized ownership fingerprint, reject malformed JSON values and normalize forbidden field names. New regression controls cover the reported bypasses; semantic paraphrases and answers hidden in prose remain outside this trusted-curator check. Existing registry databases are checked for normalized collisions when opened; incompatible legacy data fails closed. E0 mission, executed under approved caps scripts/v03_e0.py prepare verifies the pinned published source and model without inference. The frozen plan is experiments/plans/v03-e0.json; configuration is configs/v03-e0.json. Ian explicitly approved these caps; the authorization is retained in the local mission store. Caps: 30 local requests, 3,840 reserved generated tokens, 600 active seconds, 64 MiB artifacts, one inference at once, zero retries. A single fixed store contains all resume spending; none of the former mission's unused allowance is transferred. The schedule tests STOP before inference, resumes the same mission, runs the finite historical task schedule, then re-verifies in a fresh process with no new requests. Synthetic tests cover failure/restart behavior separately. The fresh v0.2.1 mission completed 30 calls, 1,008 generated tokens, 3,840 reserved tokens, and 23.125 active seconds, with 36 evidence bundles. STOP prevented all calls before resume; a fresh process reverified the evidence and decisions with zero additional calls. The fixed-tool route remains the strongest control; no policy was promoted. The full request allowance is spent. The direct route passed 3/6, learned router 5/6, fixed model-plus-tool 4/6 (rejected for regression), and deterministic tools 6/6. These are freshly executed historical synthetic families, not new independent sources or generalization. Inference latency median was 0.313s and nearest-rank p95 1.203s; peak VRAM was not sampled. The roughly 0.45 MiB local store stayed under its 64 MiB cap. E0 also exposed stale top-level status.stop_reason=kill switch after the adaptive state had finished. v03-e0-decision.json records COMPLETED_WITH_STATUS_OBSERVABILITY_DEFECT; the original runner receipt is preserved rather than silently rewritten. The v0.3 finalizer now publishes the terminal campaign reason, with a synthetic STOP/resume regression. The real evidence remains v0.2.1; this later fix is not relabeled as fresh real-model validation. A complete unqualified reliability gate is therefore not claimed. Grok also confirmed this status defect and found interrupted preflight resume, wrapper cap-verification and historical-test attribution gaps. The final wrapper requires an explicit resume for an already paused store, validates measured budget counters, and keeps preparation checks separate from historical test receipts. These repairs have synthetic coverage only. They do not modify the pinned runtime or replace the original E0 evidence. The historical code-repair tasks expose fixture_outputs in their requests; E0 therefore cannot validate the new evaluator boundary or independent generalization. The repaired wrapper was also checked against the already finished E0 store: all historical receipt/plan bytes stayed identical, spending stayed at 30 calls, and the status-defect decision reproduced. This cached check is recorded in experiments/results/v03-e0-wrapper-recheck.json and used zero new calls. E1 design and independent review The draft specifies B0/B1/B2/B4/C1, authentic source families, wrong-tool controls, source-level paired inference, and a 12-task, 24-call diagnostic pilot. Its much larger confirmatory scenarios are unapproved planning estimates. Sources, labels, calibration and empirical assumptions are missing, so E1 cannot freeze or run yet. No E2/E3 result is claimed. NVIDIA Nemotron reviewed the supplied design. We accepted its source inventory, hierarchical dependence, baseline ceiling and cost-accounting cautions. Three mathematical objections were rejected after derivation: a union bound gives P(all four succeed) = 1 - 40.05 = 0.80; a paired binary difference has Var(D) = P(D != 0) - E[D]^2; and a 0.15 planning effect over a 0.02 margin leaves 0.13 signal, not 0.15. Review text and dispositions are preserved. A model's critique is evidence to inspect, not approval by itself. Durable next work 1. Preserve the finished E0 checkpoint and consumed 30-call ceiling. Carry the observed status defect and tested v0.3 repair into the next authorized mission. 2. Integrate the registry with a development-only candidate adapter, independently owned evaluator, actual-source/config hash binding, and aggregate budget ledger. 3. Inventory genuinely independent sources and calibrate known-good/known-bad checker controls. Complete a zero-inference synthetic campaign first. 4. Review and freeze a newly authorized diagnostic pilot. A failed pilot opens a counterexample-linked hypothesis; it does not recycle its data as untouched. 5. Only after those gates, reconsider a powered E1 and chronological E2. Publication ships this engineering checkpoint and evidence. It does not deploy a learned policy, replenish inference budgets, or claim the v0.3 research goal has been achieved. Measured reproduction !Fresh v0.2.1 route comparison Read all arms, per-family results and resource limits. Source and evidence Download experimental source Source manifest E0 decision E1 draft Last verified: 21 November 2026 UTC.

title: Video mission engineering alpha
text: Video mission engineering alpha 21 November 2026 UTC · v0.3.0.dev2 · experimental. HIVE now reads a bounded local video/caption pair, normalizes captions, selects two source-backed cue proposals, verifies the results, saves development feedback and resumes from durable evidence. Outputs remain local. This is an engineering milestone; Level A is not accepted and Level B has not run. What ran A 28.32-second excerpt from a 39:13.75 studio stream completed two objective jobs (captions and clip proposals) using one local-model call and 17 generated tokens. Fresh-process replay and STOP/resume used zero additional calls. The source had prior editing exposure; editorial acceptance is pending and it does not count toward unused A2 tasks. The final runtime passed 235 tests, with 2 Windows symlink skips, and all 3 CLI end-to-end journeys. Windows junction controls passed. Independent adversarial tests terminate actual worker processes before dispatch and after output rename, then check job identity, costs and output reconciliation. A clean extracted release ZIP passed execution, fresh-process replay, STOP and resume with unchanged output bytes and zero model requests. The local adapter pins the selected model digest before transport, bounds output and context, and records actual generated tokens. Input-token measurement is unavailable. Caption normalization and clip timestamp/source verification are deterministic; they do not verify audio alignment or editorial quality. Clip proposals remain needs_operator_review. Download and reproduce - Complete source and public evidence ZIP - Operator demo instructions - Full supplied build plan - Acceptance inventory and remaining gates - Current evidence summary - Independent review decisions - Final test report - CLI journey report - Clean final ZIP receipt - Publication manifest - Exact file manifest Source commit: 2347e6add52542ef5516f680ac77b06e10f08ba2. Runtime source SHA256: e8dc974bf4e71f44879bd0a5dfe4194f09d97cd29c9c19c77be11a6be0a6631c. Download SHA256: 7c312b15b598dcde87f548aa550d57c192ab9cac34635601a0fdb0c05ebadf96. Learning and limits The mission records the development policy before and after independently verified feedback, the route used, and the next proposed route. A proposal is not counted as a later executed task. No experimental policy has been promoted. Structural feedback cannot establish whether a clip is engaging or preserves a joke. The complete Level A gate still requires a frozen inventory of at least 12 unused operator-approved tasks across video and isolated code/test, at least 10 accepted outputs, and the remaining operator/recovery evidence. Reusing cues from one stream does not create independent source families. The actual isolated repository workflow and three-family transfer study remain future work. Strong-baseline superiority and compounding improvement are unproven. The separate WP0 audit used one real local-model call (8 generated tokens) on the previously published v0.3.0.dev1 code. It is not attributed to this changed video runtime. Earlier E0 and controller experiments retain their original source versions, budgets and limitations. Next bounded work · Earlier v0.3 foundation · Experiment registry

title: HIVE v0.3.0.dev3 integration report
text: HIVE v0.3.0.dev3 integration report INTEGRATED_PROTOTYPE_DEMONSTRATED — adaptation not yet validated. One executable now connects task intake, governed tool/model execution, independent verification, persisted feedback, candidate comparison and recovery. Both genuine demonstration missions passed. The candidate then lost a critical comparison and was rejected; the next task retained the correct tool policy. Last verified: 21 November 2026 Las Vegas / 22 November UTC. Independent Terra acceptance is recorded for this bounded development workflow. Level A and Level B remain unaccepted. The public site distributes source and evidence; it is not a hosted model service. Download runnable source · Runbook · Architecture map · Publication hashes The latest source includes a separately verified crash-accounting repair. The exact source of the six-call run is archived separately. Historical results retain their original source identity. One shared execution path mermaid flowchart TD T[Scoped task] -- G[Governor and fixed P0] G -- E[Shared Executor] E -- W[Tool or pinned local model] W -- A[Artifacts and events] A -- V[Independent verifier] V -- F[Attributable development feedback] F -- C[Frozen candidate P1] C -- X[Separate comparison against controls] X -- R[Reject losing candidate] R -- N[Next task retains P0] The governor excludes prohibited, unavailable, unverifiable and over-budget routes before ranking them. Model text has no shell or filesystem authority. The candidate is separate from the governing policy; feedback cannot approve itself. Every executed route has source, task, configuration, model and policy identities attached to immutable evidence. The existing Executor, Store, verifier and Policy remain the shared implementation. These boundaries do not depend on model size. The real adapter demonstrated here is Ollama. A frontier-model adapter and evidence that HIVE improves a powerful model are future work, not established capabilities. What actually ran Stage Actual result --- --- Mission A Tool grouped real repository-source rows: core 61,800 bytes and nested 4,720 bytes. Independent reduction passed. Mission B Pinned local model classified three actual directive excerpts. All three independently frozen development labels matched. Separate inventory comparison P1 selected the local model and returned 42,073 bytes; the correct total was 41,907. Incumbent, strongest applicable fixed and learning-disabled controls used the tool and passed. Separate classification comparison All four arms returned limits for d5 where the independent label was routing; the other three labels matched. The failed verdicts and original labels are preserved. Decision REJECTED. Critical inventory regression; paired quality delta -0.5 on two development tasks against each control. No promotion. Subsequent task Governing P0 still chose the tool and correctly returned 71,415 bytes for new rows. The run made 6 local requests, produced 147 generated tokens, had 768 reserved generated tokens, and used 18.578 active seconds / 11 cycles. Ceilings were six requests, 768 tokens, 180 active seconds, 24 cycles and 64 MiB, with zero retries and one local inference globally. This allocation is spent. title: HIVE v0.3.0.dev4 readiness report
text: HIVE v0.3.0.dev4 readiness report READY_FOR_PRESSURE_TESTS.
