title: External landscape of similar systems
text: HIVE — Research Update: External Landscape of Similar Systems Database update purpose: Record external programs, software and models that work partly or wholly like HIVE, found by web research on 22 November 2026. This is a research synthesis. Nothing here was run, reproduced or measured on HIVE hardware. External results keep the scope their authors reported. Read it with the integrated design map, which places each of these parts into the HIVE design, and with the earlier 100-project catalog, which this update extends. 0. Change log — what is new ID Finding Classification Database action ------------ EXT-01 Every HIVE component has an external counterpart. No single external project was found that combines all of them. [SYNTHESIS] Add coverage map (section 4). EXT-02 The 100-project catalog does not cover the systems closest to the HIVE learning loop. Regimes, GEPA, ACE, Darwin Gödel Machine, Hyperagents, Meta-Harness, SIA, ADAS, AFlow and Agent Lightning were absent from the site search index before this update. [SOURCE] site index, 22 Nov 2026 Add entries in section 2; do not relabel old catalog outcomes. EXT-03 A published protocol now tests whether optimizer gains compound across task phases. Two of three optimizers failed it. The one that passed enforces a no-regression constraint inside the search. [SOURCE] Link to G04 and EXP-05. EXT-04 A published, open-source loop (Regimes) implements held-out-gated promotion on an event-sourced runtime. [SOURCE] Compare against the HIVE promotion governor before further governor work. EXT-05 The field now names this area "harness self-improvement" or "harness evolution". [SOURCE] Add the term to search vocabulary. EXT-06 At least four other active agent projects use the name Hive, HIVE or hive-mind. [SOURCE] Record in section 3; naming decision is open. Evidence legend - [SOURCE] Stated in the linked external page or paper. Not reproduced here. - [SYNTHESIS] Comparison or reasoning made in this update. - [VENDOR] A claim from the project's own marketing or from blog posts, with no controlled study found. - [OPEN] Not resolved by this research. - [UNREAD] Surfaced only as a citation; the primary page was not read. 1. What HIVE was compared against HIVE as published on this site: framework 0.2, coder directions 0.4, the adaptive-organization addendum, and implementation status at 0.4.0.dev1. In short: a local-first, modular organization of specialists and deterministic tools, with a capability registry, selector, execution kernel, supervisors, memory and evidence services, a learning workbench, and a release registry that promotes only candidates that pass held-out gates. Six layers can change (L1 memory, L2 procedures, L3 routing, L4 parameters, L5 topology, L6 communication). 2. Closest external systems Ordered by how much each bears on HIVE's open work. EXT-S01 — Regimes on ActiveGraph - What it is [SOURCE]: An improvement loop on an event-sourced agent runtime. It diagnoses a failed evaluation, proposes a repair at one typed point in the pipeline, and promotes it only after static checks, sandbox execution, in-sample evaluation and held-out validation. Each promote or discard is a logged event that replays deterministically. - Reported result [SOURCE]: On LongMemEval-S across five seeded splits, 44 candidates authored, 27 discarded in-sample, 2 discarded at the held-out gate, 14 promoted. Held-out gains of +0.05 to +0.10 on four splits. The author states the held-out gate rarely fires, so selection pressure is low. - Overlap with HIVE [SYNTHESIS]: promotion governor, evidence service, restart replay. - Has that HIVE lacks: a promoted held-out gain on a public benchmark; a failure taxonomy that routes each failure to a pipeline seam. - HIVE has that it lacks: multiple specialists; routing, parameters and topology as change targets. - Links: paper · code EXT-S02 — "Do Agent Optimizers Compound?" and RELAI-VCL - What it is [SOURCE]: A continual-learning evaluation. Optimize an agent on 12 Terminal-Bench 2.0 tasks, measure transfer to 10 new tasks without re-optimizing, then optimize again and check whether the first gains survive. 200 rollouts per phase. - Reported result [SOURCE]: Agent Phase 1 Transfer Final Lifelong average --------------- Baseline 62.5% 56.8% 56.8% 58.7% GEPA (prompt only) 70.8% 54.5% 72.7% 66.0% Meta-Harness 66.6% 68.2% 59.1% 64.6% RELAI-VCL 79.2% 72.7% 77.3% 76.4% - Reading [SYNTHESIS]: GEPA overfit on transfer. Meta-Harness transferred, then regressed in the second phase. Only the method with a no-regression constraint inside the search both transferred and kept improving. The authors present this as an observation on 22 tasks under one protocol, not a general law. - Overlap with HIVE: this is the design of gap G04 and of EXP-05, already specified by someone else. - Link: paper EXT-S03 — Hermes Agent (Nous Research) - What it is [SOURCE]: A self-hosted, MIT-licensed agent with a built-in learning loop. After non-trivial work it writes a skill file, revises that skill on later use, keeps searchable cross-session memory, and exports trajectories for RL training. Works with any model endpoint. - Overlap with HIVE: L2 procedural learning, the memory service, local-first operation. - Has that HIVE lacks: a large user base; a skill file format compatible with the open agent-skills convention; a reported DSPy plus GEPA route for evolving skills without a GPU. - HIVE has that it lacks [SYNTHESIS]: any gate. No held-out test stands between a skill edit and its use. - [VENDOR]: "about 40% faster on repeated research tasks" comes from blog posts. - Link: documentation EXT-S04 — Letta and Letta Code - What it is [SOURCE]: The MemGPT team's platform. Sleep-time agents reorganize memory while idle. Skill Learning turns past trajectories into skills. Learned context is versioned in git. Their stated position is that agents should learn in "token space" (prompts, skills, memory) before weights, because such changes are inspectable and portable across models. - Overlap with HIVE: the wake, capture, consolidate, evaluate cycle; L1 and L2. The existing catalog entry for MemGPT/Letta predates sleep-time agents, Skill Learning and the June 2026 "memory models" direction. - Has that HIVE lacks: git as the registry for non-parameter changes, giving diff, rollback and audit. - Their own caveat [SOURCE]: current sleep-time methods are expensive at scale and tend to overgeneralize. - Links: Skill Learning · continual learning in token space EXT-S05 — GEPA and optimize_anything - What it is [SOURCE]: An evolutionary optimizer for any text artifact (prompts, code, agent architectures, configurations). The user supplies an evaluator; the system does reflective mutation with Pareto selection. Available inside DSPy. - Overlap with HIVE: a ready-made candidate generator for the learning workbench across L2, L3, L5 and L6. - Caution [SYNTHESIS]: see EXT-S02. Unguarded, it overfit on transfer. - Link: repository EXT-S06 — Darwin Gödel Machine, Hyperagents, Meta-Harness, SIA - What they are [SOURCE]: The research line on agents that rewrite their own scaffold. DGM keeps a growing archive of self-modified coding agents. Hyperagents makes the improvement mechanism itself editable. Meta-Harness treats harness design as an outer-loop search. SIA updates the harness and then the weights of the same agent. - Overlap with HIVE: SIA changes L2/L3 and L4 in one loop, the nearest match to the HIVE state tuple. Hyperagents bears on D09. - HIVE has that they lack [SYNTHESIS]: local-first operation and evidence-status discipline. These systems optimize against benchmarks with frontier API models. - [UNREAD]: Huxley-Gödel Machine, Group-Evolving Agents, RRSI, Harness², Hierarchical Self-Improvement. - Links: Hyperagents · SIA EXT-S07 — ACE (Agentic Context Engineering) - What it is [SOURCE]: Treats an agent's context as an evolving playbook updated by generate, reflect and curate steps, using small incremental edits. Names two failure modes: brevity bias and "context collapse", where repeated rewriting erodes detail. Reports +10.6% on agent tasks and +8.6% on a finance benchmark. - Overlap with HIVE: L1 and L2 updates without parameter changes. - Link: paper EXT-S08 — Topology search: ADAS, AFlow, MaAS, GPTSwarm, EvoAgentX - What they are [SOURCE]: Methods that search over multi-agent workflow structure. ADAS frames design as search over code. AFlow uses tree search over reusable operators. EvoAgentX packages TextGrad, AFlow and MIPRO in one open-source platform. - Overlap with HIVE: L5, and finding NEW-01 of the adaptive addendum (organization as a learnable component). This is an established subfield with baselines. - Links: EvoAgentX · survey of self-evolving agents EXT-S09 — Parameter-side tools: Agent Lightning, Doc-to-LoRA, Text-to-LoRA - Agent Lightning [SOURCE]: Collects traces from an existing agent through a model proxy and trains with RL, prompt optimization or fine-tuning, with almost no change to the agent code. Can target one agent inside a multi-agent system. - Doc-to-LoRA and Text-to-LoRA [SOURCE]: A hypernetwork that produces a LoRA adapter from a document or a task description in one forward pass. Public checkpoints exist for small base models. - Overlap with HIVE: L4. The gap page records no training checkpoint. - Links: Agent Lightning · Doc-to-LoRA EXT-S10 — Aden Hive - What it is now [SOURCE]: A model-agnostic runtime in which a persistent "Queen" agent does one unit of work and spawns worker clones, coordinated through a shared tracker ledger and a persistent plan. Crash-safe park and resume, cost enforcement, human escalation. Apache 2.0. - Shift [SOURCE] fork READMEs: Earlier descriptions say a coding agent generates a node graph and the framework evolves the graph on failure. The current upstream README says there is no graph and leads with the harness. - Overlap with HIVE: execution kernel, supervisors, budgets. - HIVE has that it lacks [SYNTHESIS]: differentiated specialists (its workers are clones), held-out gates, a learning workbench, parameters. - Link: repository EXT-S11 — Ruflo Already named in the framework as a possible execution adapter. - Claims [SOURCE]: swarm topologies, queen and worker roles, a Q-learning router, a pattern learner (SONA), ReasoningBank, EWC++. - Check first [SOURCE] third-party review: The project's own May 2026 self-audit is reported as putting about 195 of 240 tools in real code, with agent execution, hive-mind transport, workflow runtime and neural prediction listed as stubbed. - Links: repository · review EXT-S12 — MELD - What it is [SOURCE]: Recursive self-improvement for multi-agent scientific discovery, scored by private evaluators that run outside the agent workspace. Labels, evaluator state and scoring files are inaccessible to the agents and restored before each validation. - Overlap with HIVE: the open "stronger evaluator isolation" gap. - Link: paper 3. Other projects using the name Project What it is Note --------- Aden Hive EXT-S10 Largest by adoption. HIVE-AI (THTWASBRUTAL/HIVE-AI) Role cards, scenario checks, and seeded held-out variants so a candidate cannot pass by memorizing inputs; private seeds for real promotions. Close in spirit to HIVE quarantine. Only one pull request was read. HivemindOS Local-first control room for agent fleets across a user's own machines, with a shared Obsidian vault. Has a crypto token named HIVE. Ruflo hive-mind mode Queen and worker swarm mode. EXT-S11. Apache Hive, Hive blockchain Unrelated. Dominate plain web searches for "hive". The naming decision is [OPEN]. 4. Coverage map HIVE part Closest external work In the 100 catalog before this update --------- Promotion governor, quarantine, rollback Regimes, RELAI-VCL, HIVE-AI No Learning workbench (candidate generation) GEPA, DGM, Meta-Harness AlphaEvolve only Procedures from experience (L2) Hermes skills, Letta Skill Learning, ACE Partly (Voyager, Reflexion) Sleep and consolidation Letta sleep-time agents; Google sleep and Nested Learning Google yes; Letta partly Topology as learnable (L5) ADAS, AFlow, MaAS, GPTSwarm, EvoAgentX No Parameters from traces (L4) Agent Lightning, SIA, Doc-to-LoRA No Selector and routing (L3) RouteLLM, FrugalGPT, Ruflo router Yes Execution kernel, leases, resume Aden Hive, Temporal, LangGraph Yes, except Aden Evaluator isolation MELD No Compounding test "Do Agent Optimizers Compound?" No 5. What was not found elsewhere These look like HIVE's own contribution. None is demonstrated. Current status records no beneficial-learning gain and no promotion. - Six separate change layers under one registry, with each improvement record naming the layer changed. - Four separated channels, including a teaching channel where admission and evaluation precede promotion. - Evidence-status labels on every claim, and publication of rejected candidates as results. - The "use both" rule for organizational modes as an explicit requirement. - Local-first operation on consumer hardware. 6. What external systems have that HIVE does not yet 1. A promoted held-out improvement (Regimes, RELAI-VCL). 2. Results on a public benchmark, so numbers can be compared. 3. An off-the-shelf candidate generator. 4. Git as the registry for non-parameter changes. 5. A skill format other tools can read. 6. Trace capture decoupled from the agent. 7. Users who find failures. 7. Limits of this research - External results were read, not reproduced. - The HIVE-AI repository page and Lilian Weng's July 2026 survey "Harness engineering for self-improvement" could not be opened. Several papers above cite the survey. - The 100 existing catalog entries and their historical outcome labels were not rechecked. - Adoption and speed figures for Hermes and Ruflo are [VENDOR]. - Earlier chat-only HIVE research that was not supplied as a file is not included here.

title: Integrated design map
text: HIVE — Integrated Design Map Purpose: Place each external part from the external landscape update into the HIVE design as one whole. This is a design proposal. Nothing here is implemented or measured. It does not change coder directions 0.4, approve any experimental policy or weights, or authorize new model calls. Existing alternatives and open decisions stay open. Sources of the HIVE side: the framework, the adaptive addendum, the gap and change plan, known gaps and implementation status. 1. The whole in one picture HIVE already has two loops. The external parts fit into the slow loop and around the gate. The fast loop needs little from outside. mermaid flowchart TD A[Task and constraints] -- B[Selector and budgets] B -- C[Specialists and tools] C -- D[Independent verification] D -- E[Result and evidence] E -- F[Event log] F -- G[Failure routing] G -- H[Candidate generator] H -- I[Static checks and sandbox] I -- J[Development evaluation] J -- K[Private held-out evaluation] K -- L{No regression and gain?} L --No M[Reject and publish] L --Yes N[Versioned release with rollback] N -- B N -- O[Compounding check on new tasks] O -- F Where the external parts sit: Box HIVE name External part Stance ------------ Event log Evidence service, restart replay Regimes / ActiveGraph event sourcing Study, compare Failure routing Credit assignment Regimes failure-to-seam taxonomy Adapt Candidate generator Learning workbench GEPA, ACE-style edits, skill extraction Adopt behind the gate Static checks, sandbox, development, held-out Decider D5 Regimes four-stage gate Already aligned; compare Private held-out evaluation Evaluator isolation MELD private evaluators, HIVE-AI seeded variants Adapt No regression and gain Promotion governor RELAI-VCL no-regression constraint Adopt as a rule Versioned release Release registry Git for non-parameter layers (Letta) Adopt Compounding check Gap G04, EXP-05 Two-phase protocol Adopt as an experiment Selector and budgets Deciders D1, D2 Nothing new needed Keep Specialists and tools Execution kernel Aden Hive, Ruflo Study only 2. Stance on each external part Four stances: adopt (use as is), adapt (take the idea, build to HIVE contracts), study (compare before deciding), decline (does not fit now). Part Stance Why --------- Two-phase compounding protocol Adopt Closes G04 with a published design. Small. Needs no new architecture. No-regression rule inside candidate search Adopt The only method that compounded in that study. Matches D5. Git-versioned L1/L2/L3/L5/L6 artifacts Adopt Diff, rollback and audit for text-shaped changes at no build cost. GEPA as candidate source Adopt behind the gate Removes hand-built candidate code. Overfits when unguarded. Regimes gate order and event shape Study, then adapt Nearest reference implementation of the governor. Failure-to-seam routing Adapt Tells the workbench which layer a failure belongs to. Private evaluators outside the workspace Adapt Addresses the open evaluator-isolation gap. Seeded held-out variants Adapt Cheap protection against memorized fixtures. Open skill file format for L2 Adapt Makes HIVE procedures readable by other harnesses and theirs by HIVE. ACE incremental edits Adapt Guards against context collapse in L1 and L2. Sleep-time consolidation (Letta) Study One more arm for EXP-06 and D03; not a replacement for the existing sleep research paths. Topology search (AFlow, ADAS, MaAS) Study Baselines for EXP-01 and L5. Use as comparison arms first. Agent Lightning trace capture Study Useful once an L4 experiment is justified. Doc-to-LoRA, Text-to-LoRA Study, later Cheapest L4 route, but only after a non-parameter promotion succeeds. Aden Hive as kernel Study Overlaps the least novel part of HIVE. Compare on one mission before any commitment. Ruflo learning features Study with caution Reported stubs; verify each feature before relying on it. DGM, Hyperagents (self-editing meta level) Decline for now Conflicts with the separation-of-duties rule unless the gate stays outside the editable surface. Keep as a research path under D09. Hermes ungated skill edits Decline No test between an edit and its use. Take the format, not the policy. 3. By learning layer Layer Current HIVE state Part to bring in Gate before promotion ------------ L1 memory Local memory contracts with provenance, expiry, correction, rollback tests Incremental edits (ACE); idle-time consolidation as a test arm Retention and stale-error checks; EXP-04, EXP-06 L2 procedures One failure-to-procedure cycle exercised; candidate rejected Skill file format; GEPA or skill extraction as source D5; held-out tasks; no regression on prior procedures L3 routing Static router; learned router quarantined (P2) No-regression search; failure-to-seam routing Unused holdout, not reused validation L4 parameters No checkpoint Trace capture; hypernetwork adapters Only after an L2 or L3 promotion; separate approval for training L5 topology Proposed Topology-search methods as comparison arms EXP-01, EXP-07 with matched budgets L6 communication Four channels specified Nothing external found that matches EXP-04 4. By decider - D1 eligibility: unchanged. - D2 routing: unchanged. External routers are already in the catalog. - D3 verification value: add seeded variants as a cheap verifier-robustness check. - D4 learning priority: failure-to-seam routing gives D4 a layer to assign each failure to. - D5 promotion: add an explicit no-regression condition evaluated during candidate search, not only at the end; add a compounding check after promotion. Both are proposals. 5. By experiment and decision HIVE item External input Effect --------- EXP-05 compounding future learning Two-phase protocol and its four reported arms Gives a ready design and reference numbers under a different setting EXP-01 organization without weight changes AFlow, ADAS, MaAS as arms Stronger baselines than a static orchestration EXP-06 rehearsal and consolidation Idle-time consolidation; context-collapse control One more arm; one more failure measure Gap G04 Same as EXP-05 Moves from planned to specified Gap: evaluator isolation MELD, HIVE-AI Concrete patterns to test D02 where learning persists Token-space-first argument (Letta); harness-then-weights (SIA) Two external positions to record; neither settles it D09 how far self-improvement may reach Hyperagents An example of the far end; keep the gate outside D11 what constitutes verification Regimes four-stage gate A comparable definition 6. Proposed build order Ordered by return for effort. Each step has an acceptance condition. None is approved by this page. 1. Compounding experiment on the existing harness. Two task phases, a transfer score before re-optimizing, a final score, and a lifelong average, with an unchanged control. Accept when: the protocol runs end to end with frozen task sets and the result, positive or negative, is published. 2. No-regression condition in the candidate loop. Accept when: a candidate that improves the new slice and regresses a prior one is rejected by a test. 3. Regimes comparison note. Read its code and record where the HIVE event log and gate differ. Accept when: a decision record states borrow, keep or merge for each difference. 4. Git registry for non-parameter artifacts. Accept when: a promoted or rejected L2 or L3 artifact has a commit, a diff and a tested rollback. 5. Evaluator moved outside the candidate workspace, with seeded variants. Accept when: a candidate process cannot read labels or evaluator state, shown by a failing access test. 6. External candidate generator behind the gate. Accept when: generated candidates pass through the same D5 path as hand-built ones and at least one is rejected for overfitting. 7. Skill file format for L2. Accept when: one existing HIVE procedure round-trips through the format. 8. Topology arms for EXP-01. Accept when: at least one searched topology and one static baseline run under matched budgets. 9. First L4 experiment. Only after a non-parameter promotion. Needs separate approval. Steps 1 to 5 need no new external dependency beyond reading one repository. 7. Invariants this map keeps - An experimental agent cannot modify its own acceptance gates or approve its own changes. - Private evaluator stores and per-case holdout labels and results stay out of public exports. - Rejected candidates and failures are published with their scope. - Proposal, implementation, execution, measurement and interpretation stay separate. - The 100, 1,000 and 10,000 logical-expert paths and all competing organizations stay open. - Nothing here authorizes model calls, training or promotion. 8. Open questions - Does the HIVE event log already carry what Regimes relies on for deterministic replay, or is a cache of model responses missing? - Which public benchmark, if any, should HIVE report on so results can be compared? Local models may be too weak for Terminal-Bench 2.0 as published. - Is the kernel comparison (current kernel, Ruflo adapter, Aden Hive) worth a mission, given the kernel is not where HIVE differs? - Naming: keep HIVE with a qualifier, or change it. 9. Inputs not included Earlier HIVE research that exists only in chat and was not supplied as a file is not part of this map. Supply it and it can be merged under the existing merge rules.

title: Owner decisions — 22 November 2026
text: HIVE — Owner decisions, 22 November 2026 Purpose: Record the decisions Ian Myers gave on 22 November 2026 in response to the integrated design map. Where an answer was a plain "yes" to a question with several options, the reading taken is stated and marked [READING] so it can be corrected. This page grants no runtime authority. The runtime accepts live inference only from a separate operator approval file created locally; publishing a decision here does not create one. Decided Question Decision Consequence ------------ 1 Publish the external landscape and design map Yes Merged to main on 22 November 2026. 2 Compounding experiment next Yes The two-phase protocol becomes the next experiment. Design it so Level A tasks can serve as phase one. 3 Approve new local-model calls Yes [READING] Read as: the existing written O5 proposal (8 tasks, at most 24 requests, 128 generated tokens each, 3,072 total, one request at a time, 1,800 active seconds, 64 MiB). A budget for the compounding experiment is agreed in principle; its numbers are not yet written. The operator still has to create the approval file locally. 4 No-regression condition inside candidate search Yes Add to the candidate loop. The review gate already requires no_regression at the end; this moves the check earlier as well. 5 Regimes: borrow, keep or merge Yes [READING] Read as: write the one-page comparison first, then take specific pieces while keeping HIVE's structure. 6 Git registry for non-parameter artifacts Yes Alongside the existing manifest, which records the commit. 7 Evaluator outside the candidate workspace; seeded variants Yes Required before any promotion is claimed. 8 External candidate generator behind the gate Yes After 4 and 7 are in place. 9 Report on a public benchmark Yes The benchmark is not yet chosen. It must be one a local model can attempt. 10 Execution kernel Compare in detail See the kernel comparison. A measured comparison on one mission is still unrun. 11 Self-editing of the improvement mechanism Not now, but lay the base now See the base for later self-improvement. D09 stays open as research. 12 Ungated skill edits Decline; take the file format only No ungated lane. 13 Open skill file format for procedures Yes One existing procedure should round-trip through the format. 14 When parameter training starts After a non-parameter promotion succeeds Needs its own approval when the time comes. Not yet decided - 15. The name (keep, add a qualifier, or rename). - 16. Individual catalog pages for the new external systems. - 17. Whether earlier chat-only research will be supplied for merging. - The compounding experiment's inference budget. - The public benchmark. Order that follows from these decisions 1. Operator creates the local approval for the existing O5 proposal. 2. Compounding experiment specified with frozen task sets and a written budget. 3. No-regression condition in the candidate loop. 4. Regimes comparison note. 5. Git registry; evaluator isolation with seeded variants. 6. The mutability manifest from the base for later self-improvement, because it is cheapest before more learned artifacts exist. 7. External candidate generator; skill file format. 8. Public benchmark chosen and run. Earlier pages keep their original text. Where this record differs from a proposal on the integrated design map, this record governs.

title: Execution kernel comparison
text: HIVE — Execution kernel comparison Purpose: Compare, in detail, the three candidates for the part of HIVE that starts work, tracks it, recovers it and enforces limits. Requested by owner decision 10. Method and limits: Source and documentation were read on 22 November 2026. Nothing was installed or run. No mission was executed on any of the three, so there are no speed, quality or cost measurements here. Versions read: the HIVE 0.4.0.dev1 published source ZIP; Aden Hive at its 17 November 2026 commit (package version 1.0.15); Ruflo at its 22 November 2026 commit (package claude-flow 3.80.1). Ruflo was surveyed, not read in depth. 1. What each one is HIVE kernel. A small Python service with no runtime dependencies. A SQLite store holds jobs and content-addressed artifacts. One executor claims a job, checks it against pre-declared routes and budgets, runs it, has a deterministic verifier measure the result, and records evidence. It does not run code written by a model. Its purpose is to make every result checkable. Aden Hive. An agent runtime built on one primitive, the agent loop. A long-lived "queen" agent does the first unit of work herself, saves the method as a skill, then starts worker clones in parallel. Workers write rows to a shared SQLite "tracker" table, and the queen checks progress with SQL. Its purpose is to get many similar units of real work done reliably. Ruflo. A Node and Rust orchestration layer built around Claude Code and Codex as the execution host, with swarm modes, a router and memory features. Its purpose is to coordinate many coding-assistant agents. 2. Side by side Dimension HIVE kernel 0.4.0.dev1 Aden Hive 1.0.15 Ruflo 3.80.1 ------------ Language and runtime Python, standard library only Python 3.11+, Node 20+ for the dashboard Node 20+, TypeScript, Rust crates Size About 13,600 lines of Python including scripts About 125,000 lines of Python in core, excluding tests Large; not counted Dependencies None pydantic, anthropic, litellm, mcp, fastmcp, croniter, psutil, more for tools Many; tied to Claude Code or Codex License Yours Apache 2.0 MIT Unit of execution A job on a pre-declared route (tool, model call, or fixed workflow) An agent loop that chooses its own tool calls An agent session in the host assistant Who decides the next step The governor, from a finite list of feasible routes The model, turn by turn The model and swarm coordinator Parallel work One worker at a time, enforced by a lock Worker clones, four at a time by default, others queued Swarm topologies Shared state Job table plus immutable artifacts Tracker table the queen defines; workers upsert one row per unit Shared memory store Crash recovery Leases with owner and generation; recover(); restart replay checked with unchanged budget Every agent saves state to disk and resumes; "what's left" is a fresh tracker query Not verified Batch runs Not present Playbooks with retry, backoff, rate-limited lanes and a dead-letter list Not verified Budgets Finite request, token, time and memory ceilings; operator approval file needed for live inference Hard limits on turns and tool calls per worker; no limit in dollars Not verified Isolation of risky work Docker adapter for code; model-written code is not executed Built-in tools, including shell, run inside the Hive process; no Docker image Not verified Models Local Ollama on loopback only Any LiteLLM provider, including Ollama Hosted assistants first Tools and integrations A few deterministic tools Shell, files, search, PDF, scraping, browser bridge, any MCP server MCP tools; a third-party review reports a share are stubs Scheduling None Cron, interval and webhook triggers Not verified Human in the loop STOP and resume in a local console; approvals by file Colony approval, inbox, Telegram and Slack escalation Not verified Independent verification Deterministic verifier separate from the runner; reviewer must differ from author The queen checks worker rows; an optional judge can ask for a retry Not verified Held-out promotion gate Yes. Fail-closed; nine required evidence flags; at least 24 matched held-out tasks with a positive confidence bound None found None found Learning across sessions Finite route selector updated from development feedback only; candidates quarantined until gated Memory notes, learned skills, playbooks. Its documentation states there is no graph and no cross-generation code rewriting Claimed router and pattern learning Skill format Own records Open Agent Skills format Own formats Evidence and audit Hashes, provenance, publication manifests, rejected candidates kept Tracker rows and session files Not verified Users and upkeep You Active company and community Active 3. What differs in kind 1. Who is trusted. HIVE trusts a verifier and a gate, and treats the model as a part that must prove its output. Aden trusts the queen to check her workers. That is the difference between a measured system and a managed one. 2. What the model may do. In HIVE the model picks from routes someone declared. In Aden the model writes its own next step, including shell commands, inside the same process. HIVE's rule against executing model-written code and Aden's in-process shell are not compatible without a sandbox around Aden. 3. What "improves" means. Aden says its mechanisms make a colony more reliable on problems it has already met, not more capable in general, and it retired graph evolution in version 1. HIVE's claim is exactly the one Aden stepped back from: improvement that is tested and compounds. 4. Scale of work. Aden is built for dozens of similar units in parallel with resume. HIVE runs one job at a time. 4. What HIVE's kernel lacks that Aden has Ranked by usefulness to HIVE. 1. A tracker table as the source of truth for a batch, so "what is left" is a query and re-running resumes. 2. Bounded parallel workers with a queue. 3. Playbooks: a deterministic runner over rows with retry, backoff and dead-letter. 4. Pilot first, then fan out: do one unit, record the method, then repeat it. 5. The open skill file format (already owner decision 13). 6. Escalation to a person through a messaging channel when a run stalls. 7. Triggers for scheduled runs. 8. A model gateway covering many providers. 5. What Aden lacks that HIVE's kernel has 1. A held-out promotion gate and a release registry with rollback for learned artifacts. 2. Separation of evaluator answers from the worker. 3. Differentiated specialists and deterministic experts. Its workers are clones. 4. Finite, operator-approved inference budgets. 5. Isolation for code execution. 6. A zero-dependency core that can be read in a day. 6. Options Option What changes Gain Cost and risk ------------ A. Keep the HIVE kernel; port patterns 1 to 4 from section 4 A tracker table, a worker pool and a playbook runner added to the existing store and executor Parallel batch work without giving up the gate, budgets or isolation You build and test it. A few hundred lines each, by estimate. B. Run Aden Hive as one route behind the HIVE kernel HIVE treats a colony as a specialist: it hands over a bounded task, then verifies the output independently Aden's tools, browser and parallelism at once A large dependency; its shell tools need a container around them; its internal steps are not HIVE evidence C. Replace the HIVE kernel with Aden Hive HIVE's gate, evidence and approval rebuilt on top of Aden Community upkeep of the runtime Loses the property that every step is declared and checked; biggest rework; ties HIVE to another project's direction, which already changed once D. Ruflo as the base — — Wrong fit: Node-based, built around hosted coding assistants, with reported stubs. Keep only as the optional adapter already named in the framework 7. Assessment [SYNTHESIS] Option A fits the design best. The kernel is where HIVE's guarantees live, and neither alternative has them. Option B is worth one trial later as a way to borrow tools, with Aden inside a container and treated as an unverified specialist. Option C gives up what makes HIVE different. Option D is not recommended. This is a reading of source, not a measurement. The mission comparison in owner decision 10 is still unrun and would need its own approved budget. 8. Open - Whether a single-writer SQLite store holds up under a worker pool, or needs a queue in front. - Whether parallel local-model calls help at all on one GPU, where requests are served one at a time. - Whether Aden Hive's agent loop can be driven with a fixed tool allowlist tight enough to meet HIVE's boundary rules.

title: Base for later self-improvement
text: HIVE — Base for later self-improvement of the improver Purpose: Owner decision 11 is: not now, but if a piece must be in the architecture now to make it possible later, give it a good base now. This page names those pieces. It is a design proposal. It does not allow HIVE to edit its own improvement mechanism, and D09 stays open. 1. What "the improver improving itself" would mean Today the slow loop has fixed parts: how failures are triaged, how candidates are generated, how they are searched, and how they are judged. Self-improvement of the improver means some of those parts become candidates themselves. Outside examples are the Darwin Gödel Machine and Hyperagents (see the external landscape). The risk is specific: a system that can change how it is judged can learn to pass by weakening the judge. 2. What has to be true first Seven conditions. For each: whether the 0.4.0.dev1 source already meets it, by inspection on 22 November 2026. Condition Why it must come first Today ------------ 1 A mutability class on every artifact: frozen, gated, or free Without a declared boundary, "what may the system change" is answered by accident Not found as an explicit field 2 The judge lives in the frozen class and outside the candidate's reach: gate code, evaluator data, budgets, approval records A self-editing system must be physically unable to touch its referee Partly. The review gate is a pure fail-closed function and the interface cannot create an approval. Stronger evaluator isolation is an open gap and now decided (decision 7) 3 The improver's own parts are versioned artifacts: triage rules, candidate generator, search settings, prompts Something that is code baked into the kernel cannot be proposed, compared or rolled back Not yet. They are source modules 4 A seventh layer ID reserved for "improver", beside the six existing layers Every improvement record names the layer changed. Adding a layer later means re-labelling history Not present 5 A full lineage archive: every candidate keeps a pointer to its parent, including rejected ones Self-improving search needs to branch from old variants, not only the current champion Rejected candidates are kept. Parent pointers were not found by text search 6 A measure of the improver itself: how fast and how durably HIVE improves across task phases You cannot judge a change to the improver without a score for improving Not yet. The compounding experiment (decision 2) produces exactly this 7 Approval authority by class of change A change to the improver should need a higher authority than a change to a procedure Partly. The gate requires a reviewer distinct from the author. Classes of authority were not found "Not found" means not found by reading and text search of the published source. Confirm against the working tree. 3. What to build now Only the pieces that are cheap now and expensive to retrofit. 1. Mutability manifest. One file listing every artifact type with its class. Gate, evaluator, budget ceilings, approval files and this manifest itself are frozen. Procedures, routing policy, memory rules, topology and protocols are gated. Scratch and development outputs are free. A test fails the build if a frozen path changes without a human-signed record. 2. Layer ID L7 improver, reserved and unused. Records may carry it; nothing may be promoted under it. 3. parent_id on every candidate record, including rejected ones. 4. Improver settings read from a versioned file instead of constants: triage thresholds, candidate count, search budget. No behaviour change; they simply become data. 5. Authority field on promotion records, with values such as gate, independent_reviewer, owner. L7 requires owner. 6. Compounding score recorded per release once the experiment exists, so the improver has a baseline. None of these changes what HIVE does today. They change what is written down. 4. What stays closed - No candidate may be promoted under L7. - Nothing in the frozen class may be proposed as a candidate. - No external self-editing system is adopted. 5. Conditions to reopen Reconsider when all of these hold: - at least one non-parameter promotion has passed the full gate; - the compounding experiment has a published result with an unchanged control; - evaluator isolation is shown by a failing access test; - the mutability manifest has caught at least one attempted change in testing. 6. Open - Whether search strategy and triage should be one artifact or several. - Whether the frozen class should be enforced by file permissions, a separate process, or a separate machine.

title: First live local-model demo
text: HIVE v0.4 — first live local-model demo, 22 November 2026 Result: O5 PASS. Candidate REJECTED. P0 unchanged. Replay made zero model calls. 5 of the 24 approved requests were used (73 of 3,072 tokens, 7 cycles). This is the first run of the v0.4 prototype with real local-model inference. It followed the owner's chat approval of the small finite allocation proposed on the operational prototype page: 24 requests, 128 generated tokens each, 3,072 tokens in total, one worker, one pinned local classification model. What ran Step Result ------ Doctor Exit 0; model and Docker healthy Development data mission VERIFIED Python label mission (Docker) COMPLETED; patch VERIFIED Model-backed combined mission COMPLETED; data, Python, review and report stages all VERIFIED Classification learning comparison REJECTED: the candidate was identical to P0, quality tied, and it did not beat the fixed team. P0 unchanged Subsequent distinct task FAILED check_failed: the model output was shape-valid but wrong, and the independent verifier caught it STOP / resume Exit 0 Fresh-process replay of all four Identical statuses; counters unchanged Store totals after the run: 5 requests, 73 tokens, 7 cycles. Before and after replay the totals were identical (5 / 73 / 7), so replay spent nothing. Gate reading - O5 now PASS: a new authorized local dispatch with receipts. O1–O10 engineering gates all have evidence. - The release label is not yet relabeled OPERATIONAL_PROTOTYPE_DEMONSTRATED. Independent review of this run is still pending. - The failed subsequent task is kept as a result. It shows the independent verifier doing its job on a plausible but wrong model answer. What this does not show - No beneficial learning (R1). The candidate tied P0 and was rejected. - Level A not accepted (R2). It still needs six unused data sources and six unused Python snapshots, with at least 10 of 12 accepted. - Level B untested. It needs at least 24 source-disjoint held-out tasks. - No promotion. P0 remains the governing policy and P2 stays quarantined. - The run used first-party development inputs, not an untouched research corpus. Owner decisions recorded the same day - Local-model calls: approved, limited to the small proposal above. - Compare external regimes, then take pieces; keep HIVE's own kernel. See the decision record. - Compounding budget "max" is read as the full approved allocation per phase. Anything beyond it needs a new approval file. - Public benchmark: yes; the choice is delegated to the overseer and must be attemptable by the local model. - Name: no answer, so it stays HIVE. Next actions 1. Independent review of this run, then decide on the release relabel. 2. Level A needs 12 unused, approved sources from the owner. 3. See the unified integration campaign for what was built afterwards, with zero further model calls. Source revision: f5fbb1a of the HIVE repository. Private evaluator stores and per-case holdout labels and results are not published.

title: Unified integration campaign
text: HIVE unified integration — 22 November 2026 Status: ENGINEERING_INTEGRATION (INTEGRATION_TESTED). Full suite 689 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed at 25f19b2. Zero model calls and $0 of HIVE runtime spend. No Level A acceptance, no learning claim, P2 still quarantined. Baseline was 59d9b5e, the live-demo record. Version is still 0.4.0.dev1; dev4 and dev6 artifacts are untouched, and P0 governs. What was built One HIVE-native architecture: Store, Executor and ContextPolicy stay canonical, and new modules extend them. No second coordinator, daemon or database was added. Module Role State --------- Dispatch gate Runs the fail-closed context preflight before every real Ollama request and appends to the usage ledger after it. Replay and tool routes are never gated Wired, integration-tested (32afa0e) Usage ledger Hash-chained record of requests and tokens; unknown model raises Wired via the dispatch gate (7de5957) Run states Durable job transitions and effect receipts in the existing Store SQLite Wired into the Executor (25f19b2) Role registry Role deny checks; the builder role holds model dispatch Checked in the dispatch gate (25f19b2) Checkpoint promote Requires a passing review-gate verdict; rollback only to a previously promoted checkpoint Gate in place; no production code promotes (tests assert it) Decision gateway Typed decisions, including MODEL_ROUTE Reachable from the CLI only; not on the dispatch path repo_intel Selective remote git tree/fetch with blob-hash verification, https only Standalone, unit-tested OODA controller Bounded experiments with a hash-chained step log; wall-clock limit enforced Unit-tested; no production driver RunAnywhere and Obscura adapters Optional adapters OFF; both refuse to run even when enabled Campaign commits, in order: fac5586, 7de5957, e3bc72b, caa0ebe, 6e67d49, b5a025c, 21c3e96, 32afa0e, a6952cf, 25f19b2. A passing unit test does not mean a gate protects a run: modules marked standalone, CLI-only or no-driver above are not on any live path. Tests Point Result ------ Earlier reported 488 passed, 3 skipped 32afa0e (conductor-run) 661 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed 25f19b2 (worker-run, 36:52) 689 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed; the 86 focused final-wave tests were re-run by the conductor and pass A short temporary directory is needed on Windows, because long test paths hit MAX_PATH. Evidence - Preflight blocks with zero usage recorded. - Role deny, path traversal, repo-transport and binary/oversize guards are in place. - Hash-chain tamper detection covers the ledger, run events and OODA steps. - Rollback is allowed only to a previously promoted checkpoint. - The conductor reviewed every patch before commit and fixed: wrong repositories in the sources lock, a ledger chain race, a repo_intel remote-transport and -C bug, an OODA missing-verifier hole, a request-cap key bug, and a wrong store path in the audit. - Upstream decisions: all nine upstream projects are pattern-only and no code was imported. One is GPL-3.0, so no code may be copied. Two projects have license NOASSERTION and one has no SPDX license; each needs a written license review before anything moves in. Limitations - Level A: NOT ACCEPTED. It needs six unused data sources and six unused Python snapshots, with at least 10 of 12 accepted. Not attempted here. - Level B: UNTESTED. It needs at least 24 source-disjoint holdouts. - Learning is unproven. The only comparison (the live demo) tied and was rejected. - P2 is quarantined. P0 is the governing policy; no production path promotes. - The cross-process ledger lock is missing: the ledger uses an in-process lock only, so two processes could fork the chain. - Worker-agent token spend was not measured. The usage ledger governs HIVE runtime only. - The context A/B comparison was not run in this campaign. - Grok was removed mid-campaign because it stalls on larger context. Fable was not used. Next actions 1. Wire the decision gateway MODEL_ROUTE at dispatch as an explicit, reviewed route change. 2. Add a cross-process file lock to the usage ledger. 3. Add an OODA driver for one bounded experiment, using repo_intel as its first real use. 4. Record written license reviews for the NOASSERTION and no-SPDX upstreams. 5. Level A needs the owner to supply 12 unused, approved sources. Source revision: f5fbb1a of the HIVE repository (code 25f19b2). Publication grants no runtime authority and does not promote a quarantined policy or expand any budget. Private evaluator stores and per-case holdout labels and results are not published.

title: Autonomous experiment checkpoint
text: HIVE v0.4.x autonomous experiment checkpoint — 23 November 2026 Label: ENGINEERING_AUTONOMOUS_EXPERIMENT_DEMONSTRATED. Acceptance gates A1 to A9 are recorded as passing, with independent review of the new experiment and one test flake disclosed. Last code commit 89a1118; checkpoint commit 2e23f05. The runtime made zero model calls and spent $0 on inference. This builds on the unified integration campaign (689 tests at 25f19b2) and the live local-model demo. What this label means A tool-only experiment loop ran end to end on a real pinned public source: it proposed a candidate, evaluated it against baselines, and recorded an honest decision. It survived STOP, restart and replay with no duplicate effects, and the log is hash-linked. This is an engineering result about the loop. It is not evidence that the system learns. Not earned: BENEFICIAL_LEARNING_DEMONSTRATED, LEVEL_A_ACCEPTED, LEVEL_B_ACCEPTED. Tests On 89a1118 the full suite gave 821 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed in about 53 minutes. The one failure is a code-isolation test that hit a 20 second subprocess timeout while the machine was under full-suite load. The file passed 27 of 27 three times in a row when run alone, so it is recorded as a load-sensitive flake, not fixed. The 3 skips pre-date this campaign. The experiment result: a negative one Arm Held-out passes (n=7) ------ Candidate (lowercase forbidden article) 5 Strongest deterministic baseline (preregistered rule) 5 P0 (incumbent, unchanged) 1 Learning-disabled control 1 Fixed-specialist route N/A: no approved model route Decision: REJECT_NO_GAIN. The candidate ties the strongest baseline, stays quarantined, and nothing was promoted. It ties because a plain regex tool makes the same repair. The result is kept as a negative result. Limits: the held-out items are engineered variants of the candidate's own source, so the gate reports that the held-out set was not unused for learning, and n=7 supports no population claim. The run used 0 model calls and 4 network requests to allowlisted pinned GitHub sources. Quarantine summary Open items are tracked with a compensating control and a lift condition each. In one line apiece: - FR-2, evaluator isolation: open, and the next task. Candidates still run in the evaluator's process, so a generated or learned candidate could in principle alter its own score. This must be fixed before any generated, learned or code candidate is run. - FR-3: the held-out items are not independent of the candidate's source. - FR-5, FR-6, FR-7: quarantined. Low-severity review findings, each with a compensating control. Level A The owner approved Option A only (tool-only, no model calls) for the Level A source set. It has not been run. Before it can run, the three JSON/YAML sources need verifiers, and the six Python snapshots need adapters and private oracles; the three CSV sources already pass their profile check. Level A will use a separate store and must never share candidates or partitions with the evolutionary campaign. Level B is untested. What is next 1. FR-2 evaluator isolation: run candidates in a separate subprocess and score in the parent, then lift FR-2. 2. Lineage design: a one-page design mapped onto the existing store and artifacts, before any code. 3. Sensory and embodied research branch (reference only): the owner set those research plans as reference only until the core structure is proven (P4). A small replay foundation exists but is parked. No hardware, motion, model calls or training. Cost HIVE runtime: 0 model requests, $0. title: M1 accepted: first verified evolutionary benefit
text: M1 accepted: first verified evolutionary benefit — 24 November 2026 This follows the evaluator isolation note. M1 is the first milestone where a registered workflow beat the existing one on held-out data. The result is verified on synthetic data. It is a narrow result, and the limits are listed below. The runtime made 0 model calls and 0 network calls. What M1 tested - Protocol: m1-row-reconcile-v1, frozen at af4b8d6. Protocol file sha256 6517f2e6…. - Question: can deterministic, type-directed search find a workflow that handles bad rows in synthetic inventory files, when the existing workflow cannot? - Search: a pinned set of thin views (identity, parse_whole, split_rows, aggregate) plus a generic each combinator. - Nominee: [split_rows, each(parse_whole), aggregate]. It was locked before the held-out set was opened. - Incumbent: W_strict = [parse_whole, aggregate]. Results Check Nominee Control Test ------:---:--- Held-out final set (F-final, 60 cases) 60/60 12/60 exact McNemar, p = 3.6e-15 Reuse after restart in a new process (F-reuse, 20 cases) 20/20 4/20 exact McNemar, p = 1.5e-5 Random search (20 draws) none type-check The incumbent passed only the 12 clean files. The margin mostly confirms the clean and defective mix, plus the nominee's exact correctness on defective files. Lifecycle checks - After a restart, the selection resolved to the nominee from stored state. - Rollback to W_strict worked, and three post-rollback cases matched the control. - Selecting a rejected variant, forged or stale receipts, and invalid proposals were all refused. - The independent oracle rejected all five wrong-output fixtures. Regression gate Full suite: 900 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed. The one failure was a test-isolation fault: a test read a process-wide Docker counter that an earlier test had already raised. It was not an M1 behaviour fault. The test was fixed and a targeted rerun passed 45. The full suite was not rerun. Versions and cost - Runtime commit: 755aa6f. - Follow-up fix 5c901a9: policy pins now hash line-ending-normalized bytes, so a fresh Windows checkout no longer fails the stale-pin check. - M1 cost: about $9.42 against a $24 cap. Cumulative: about $64 of the $120 ceiling. - Runtime: 11 container runs, $0. Limitations - Synthetic data only. No real-world data was used. - Tiny search space. Only 3 workflows type-check, out of 584 lists. This is disclosed. No claim is made about search skill. - The designers already knew the solution. each and the error channel were declared preparation, not discovery. - Arm 2 is hardcoded to W_strict rather than reached through a skill-off path. The result is the same. - An unkeyed store writer can forge records (SQ-1). M1 ran as a trusted-local experiment. - The private holdout is owned by the same OS user as the runtime. It is a gitignored folder, not a separate trust boundary. - Open findings are unchanged from M0. - No claim is made about generality, and none is made about intelligence. Next Freeze the M2 protocol for a fixed-weight local-model campaign (gpt-oss-20b) with two distinct effects. The campaign itself waits for a separate inference go. Publication grants no runtime authority, promotes no policy and expands no budget. Private evaluator material and per-case held-out labels and results are not published.

title: M2 accepted: a local model found two new effects
text: M2 accepted: a local model found two new effects (24 Nov 2026) This follows the M1 note. M2 is the first milestone where a real local model proposed the workflows. The independent reviewer accepted both effects. The result is verified on synthetic data. It is narrow, and the limits are listed below. What M2 tested - Protocol: m2-local-model-two-effects-v1, commit d4b71d2. Protocol file sha256 9767b209…. - Model: openai/gpt-oss-20b on LM Studio, localhost, one slot, Reasoning: low. The weights were fixed. The weight sha256 matched before the first call, after the last call and after the reuse run. - Task: the model proposed step lists over M1's pinned inventory plus one declared preparation step, to_json. Each proposal was checked, retained, reused after a restart, and rolled back. - Approval: Ian approved live inference on 24 Nov. The two effects - R, row-convert-v1: the file validator from M1, parse_whole, was reused as the front end for converting CSV or JSON files into canonical JSON. Nominee: [parse_whole, to_json]. - C, batch-merge-v1: merging a batch of files, with each whole bad file quarantined. Nominee: [each(parse_whole), aggregate]. Results Check R C ------:---: Held-out final set (F-final, 60 cases) 60/60 vs 0/60 for the old workflows 60/60 vs 30/60 for the strongest old workflow Reuse after restart (20 fresh cases) 20/20 vs 0/20 20/20 vs 10/20 Campaign B reproduction same digest, 20/20 same digest, 20/20 Rollback back to W_strict; 3 cases failed as expected same Integrity rejected-variant, forged, tampered and stale receipts all refused same Cross-checks: the M1 workflow scored 0/60 on both new sets, and each new nominee scored 0/60 on the other's data. A random legal search hit a correct workflow at draw 3 for R and draw 1 for C. Bounds used - Model calls: 50 of 64. - Tokens: about 220k of 900k. - Container runs: 23 of 160. - Infrastructure retries: 0. Claim With the weights unchanged, gpt-oss-20b at Reasoning: low, proposing step lists over M1's pinned inventory plus one declared preparation view (to_json), produced on its first proposal in each of four campaigns two distinct effects the starting inventory does not produce: (R) M1's whole-file validator parse_whole reused as the parsing and rejection front end of CSV/JSON-to-canonical-JSON conversion, and (C) a two-step composition, [each(parse_whole), aggregate], that merges a multi-file batch with whole-file quarantine. On fresh held-out synthetic data each passed an independently written oracle (R 60/60 vs 0/60; C 60/60 vs 30/60 for the strongest old workflow). Each was reused after a restart (20/20 vs 0/20 and 10/20), reproduced by a second campaign, and rolled back. Limitations - Tiny search space. 7 type-legal lists for R (3 correct) and 3 for C (2 correct). Random legal search finds a hit by draw 3. This shows the propose, verify, retain, reuse pipeline with a real local model. It is not search skill, and there is no claim that the model beats random search. - Type-forced discovery for R. Any use of to_json from a Source must follow parse_whole, and the prompt's output spec matches the description of to_json. The discovery is close to a type-forced reading of the prompt. to_json is new preparation, approved by the owner. - Comparators pass 0 by construction. R's comparators pass 0 by construction, and C's strongest old workflow passes only clean batches. The margin and McNemar values mostly confirm the effect exists. The per-category raw counts are the substantive evidence. - C is M1 without split_rows. C's nominee is M1's retained workflow minus split_rows. The reviewer ruled the file-level quarantine over a list of sources a distinct use. - The conductor knew both answers. One model, one prompt family, synthetic data only. - B reuse is a cache hit. Campaign B's reuse result is a cache hit on the identical digest. Reproduction means B independently proposed the same workflow. - Trust limits are unchanged. An unkeyed store writer can forge records (SQ-1). Private holdouts sit under the same OS user. - No claim is made about generality. Disclosed deviations (non-blocking) - The loaded context length (32,768) was set but not logged per campaign. Only the model id and weight sha are evidenced. - Accepted evidence holds {final_pass, n, p}. Transcript hashes and model sha are in the nominee files. - Restart checks the manifest sha, which covers the oracle hashes, rather than re-hashing oracle files. - Arm 2 resolves through a store lookup with a digest assertion, not a separate selection path. - The integration proof read the public selection set with the known solutions before any model call. The model never saw it. - Harness code is not pinned in the manifest. Git shows it unchanged between freeze and evidence. Regression gate Full suite at the acceptance boundary: 1014 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed. M1 evidence is unchanged. Two test-isolation faults were found and fixed before the run, with no change to M2 behaviour. Versions and cost - Runtime commit: 1799c58. Protocol commit: d4b71d2. - Coding agents at list price this session: about $21, including about $1.5 of pre-M2 work. Cumulative: about $85 of the $120 ceiling. - The local model and 23 container runs cost $0. Next No further work is authorised. Registered ideas: a larger inventory where search matters, a second model, and real data. Publication grants no runtime authority, promotes no policy and expands no budget. title: Operator Prototype: retained capabilities on real inputs
text: Operator Prototype: use the retained M2 capabilities on your own files (24 Nov 2026) This follows the M2 note. M2 showed that a local model could propose two workflows that HIVE then verified, kept and reused. This build puts those two kept workflows behind the ordinary HIVE operator path, so a person can launch HIVE, pick a file, run a task, get an independently checked result, restart, and run another file. What this is: a usable local operator path with evidence. What it is not: a new held-out study, Level A or Level B, general CSV/JSON support, a search-skill result, or a production approval. Launch From the runtime package root (Windows, Python 3.11+, Docker with the pinned python:3.11-slim image; no model server needed): scripts\hive-operator.cmd D:\HIVE-operator-inputs It imports the accepted capabilities (idempotent) and opens http://127.0.0.1:8765/ with a local session token. The runbook is docs/OPERATOR_RUNBOOK.md in the package. The two operations Operation Capability (from M2) Behaviour --------- Convert a file to canonical JSON row-convert-v1, steps parse_whole - to_json Any bad row rejects the whole file, with the reason. No row salvage. Merge a batch with whole-file quarantine batch-merge-v1, steps each(parse_whole) - aggregate Valid files are merged into per-group count and bytes. Each invalid file is quarantined whole, with the reason of its first failing row. Input contract (taken from the parser and the oracle, not broadened): UTF-8 without a BOM; at most 2 MiB; CSV header exactly id,group,bytes; JSON array of objects with exactly those keys; 1 to 256 rows; unique non-empty ids and non-empty groups up to 128 characters; bytes an integer from 0 to 1,000,000,000 (CSV: canonical decimal). Batches take 2 to 20 files. To make such a file from any folder there is an explicit preparation adapter, inventory-snapshot-v1 (hive operator snapshot-dir). It is engineering preparation, not a learned capability. How a task runs 1. Intake. The file is read from the permitted folder. An immutable copy and its SHA-256 go into the store. The task identity is the operation plus the ordered file names and hashes. 2. Selection. The operator registry (an append-only chain per operation) resolves the current version and re-checks its evidence every time: genome hash, receipt hash, current protocol/policy/manifest/inventory/prompt pins, the pinned accepted version, allowed scope, revocation and type fit. Anything stale, tampered, revoked, out of scope or incompatible is refused. 3. Execution. The stored genome body runs in the pinned container (no network, read-only, non-root). Zero model calls. 4. Independent check. evaluator/m2/oracle.py, written separately from the runtime, recomputes the expected output from the input bytes in a separate python -I process. Only PASS outputs are exported. 5. Result. You get the verdict, accepted and quarantined counts, the download, and an expandable trace (capability and genome, input and output digests, evaluator pin, timings, container runs). Same operation plus same files returns the saved result with no new execution, but only while the same capability is still eligible and the evaluator pin is unchanged. After a revoke or rollback it runs through selection again. Demonstration on real inputs (24 Nov) Inputs were real first-party folders of the HIVE repository (docs, configs, scripts, evaluator, src/hive), turned into inventory files by the preparation adapter. The independent reference was PowerShell's own recursive file listing of the same folders (a different tool, no HIVE code). One defective file was derived from a real one by setting one size to -5; it is labelled DERIVED-. No model saw any input. Every journey went through the real launch command and the console HTTP API, with a full process restart in the middle. Journey Result ------ Fresh conversion (68-row docs inventory) VERIFIED; oracle PASS; downloaded JSON equals the PowerShell reference Mixed batch (4 files, 1 derived defect) VERIFIED; the derived file quarantined whole ("bytes must be a canonical nonnegative decimal integer"); merged group totals equal the PowerShell reference over the 3 accepted files Unsupported inputs BOM file, one-file merge, unknown operation, path outside the folder, .txt file: each refused with a precise reason, nothing executed STOP and resume Task submitted under STOP recorded STOPPED with 0 executions; after resume the same task ran once and verified Crash mid-task Server killed while RUNNING; after restart the task shows INTERRUPTED; resubmitting ran it once and verified Restart, different input New process; the retained capability was loaded from the store and executed (+1 execution, 0 model or proposal calls), oracle PASS, matches the reference Exact replay Same task id, same artifacts, execution and container counters unchanged, replay counter +1 Rollback Rollback selected the previous permitted version, the M2 baseline, which cannot convert: the task was refused with 0 container runs. Re-select restored the accepted version and the next task verified. History kept all three events Revoke After revoking the merge capability, resubmitting the earlier verified batch was not replayed: refused, 0 executions Final counters: 7 container runs started, 6 completed executions (the 7th was the deliberately killed one), 0 model calls, 0 proposal calls, 1 replay. The same journeys were also checked in the browser UI, including a download. Stale-pin, tampered-receipt, tampered-bundle, wrong-scope and failed-verification refusals are covered by unit tests (tests/test_operator_runtime.py), not by the live journeys. Limits - Trusted local scope only. The capabilities are marked trusted_local_experiment and production_approved: false. The SQ-1 store-writer weakness and the same-user holdout boundary from M2 are unchanged. - Narrow contract. Only the id,group,bytes inventory shape. Real files of other shapes need an explicit adapter. - Rollback here is a disable. The only earlier permitted version is the M2 baseline, which cannot perform these operations. No second accepted version exists yet. - Docker image check is bounded to 5 s. On a heavily loaded PC it can fail closed (EXECUTION_FAILED); resubmitting retries. - Usability, not research. These demonstrations do not satisfy Level A, Level B or a new held-out study. The independent oracle is the same M2 oracle; the PowerShell listing is the extra outside reference. - Tested on one Windows 11 host with Docker Desktop. Review An independent read-only reviewer (Opus) returned ACCEPT WITH FIXES with no blockers. All should-fix items were fixed before packaging: replay now respects revocation and pin changes, failed checks are not cached, unverified output is never parsed or shown as a result, verifier timeouts are handled, registry writes are transactional, STOP during execution discards the output, and session tokens are redacted from the evidence. Identity <!-- identity:start -- - Runtime commit: c7683fe82f5e7a5527b5bf70b93edcde3b7d5d40 (repository hive-ai, local). Evaluated revision for the regression gate: f65d950ae3fd7dca3dbdbff9252b3567d083af87. - Regression gate on the evaluated revision: 1042 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed on f65d950 (89 min); then a one-line readiness display fix with focused tests 39 passed, 1 skipped; clean-launch of the exported package VERIFIED/PASS. - Package: HIVE_Operator_Prototype_c7683fe.zip, SHA-256 4fa79b889dae9c4e519f50b02f9dc3e959ed918b4420cd682cce60ffda227e6f. Publication manifest: operator-prototype-publication.json. - Capability bundle build/operator/capabilities_m2.json, SHA-256 8d2a608e5678ef14581819a091eab17673f4133477f78911dc5a865be123a736. Accepted genomes: convert 5ac1c937..., merge a06169a5... (pinned in configs/operator_policy.json). - Historical references: M2 runtime 1799c58, protocol d4b71d2, M2 publication PR 69. <!-- identity:end -- Cost Coding agents this build, list price: about $12 (conductor about $10.3, independent reviewer $1.5), so the cumulative estimate is about $97 of the $120 ceiling. That cumulative figure carries forward the M2 report's estimate (about $85); it is not a reconciled ledger. Runtime: 0 model calls, $0; local container runs only. Next The next pressure experiment is one bounded discovery problem chosen from real failure records, with a richer inventory where search actually matters. It is not authorised by this build.

title: Connected Goal Runner: goal to discovery to admission to reuse
text: Connected Goal Runner: HIVE finds a missing step, gets it checked, admits it and reuses it (25 Nov 2026) This follows the Operator Prototype. The Operator Prototype ran two kept workflows when you named the operation. This build lets you type a goal instead. HIVE writes a task contract, plans with the capabilities it already has, and finds the step it is missing. It asks the local model to write that step. An independent evaluator then checks the step on private cases the model never saw. After a signed admission, HIVE reuses the step on new files after a restart, with zero model calls. What this is: one connected run of the learning loop, end to end, through the normal console. What it is not: a learning advantage, Level A or Level B, neural weight learning, or a production approval. The model's step ties a simple hand-written script. The six gates Gate Result What was shown --------- C1 goal and contract PASS Convert and merge goals typed in the console become versioned task contracts and VERIFIED results, with 0 model calls. The old explicit-operation interface still works (8/8). C2 typed planning PASS Folders are planned as [snapshot, snapshot, merge] with no hand-written workflow. A revoked capability never executes. Replays are labelled, and a restart keeps provenance. C3 discovery PASS A real goal (compare before and after copies of MOM production folders) exposed the gap canonical_rows x2 - inventory_diff. Experiment d-563f4dc928c28acb7944 got one local gpt-oss-20b call. The candidate passed the independent evaluator 24/24. C4 admission and rollback PASS (rollback: test fixture) A signed admission statement admitted the step. After a restart, fresh real inputs were VERIFIED with no regeneration. Tampered, unsigned and revoked admissions were refused (14/14). C5 model dispatch PASS In active mode, a request for an unmeasured model was routed to the qualified openai/gpt-oss-20b and executed there. With the model unloaded, the request was refused as MODEL_UNAVAILABLE with 0 calls. C6 connected acceptance PASS All 13 journey steps passed on a fresh store with fresh real inputs (below). The Operator journeys still pass 9/9. C6 journey (fresh store, fresh real inputs) 1. A goal with discovery allowed produced a contract, the plan [convert, convert] and a reported gap. 2. The discovery experiment reached CANDIDATE_PASSED on the independent evaluator. 3. A signed admission created version 1 of inventory-diff. 4. The original goal was VERIFIED via [convert, convert, inventory-diff]. 5. After a console restart, a different, unused pair of folders was submitted without discovery. It was VERIFIED as retained_capability_execution, with 0 model calls, 0 proposal calls and no new experiment. 6. STOP, a kill during a run (INTERRUPTED, then resubmitted), revoke (UNRESOLVED, 0 container runs) and a 0-call budget (BUDGET_EXHAUSTED) all behaved as recorded. A one-version rollback was refused with a clear reason. Baselines: read this before the result On the 24 private cases, unchanged HIVE scores 0/24 because it has no capability for this. A hand-written scripted diff scores 24/24, and the model's candidate also scores 24/24. A matched-budget search over the M2 views cannot express the task, because no existing view produces an inventory diff. The candidate ties the scripted baseline. This is evidence that the mechanism works, not that learning beats plain code. Launch From the package root (Windows, Python 3.11+, Docker with the pinned python:3.11-slim image; LM Studio with openai/gpt-oss-20b only for discovery): scripts\hive-operator.cmd <inputs folder [port] CLI: python -m hive --store .hive\operator operator goal "TEXT" SOURCES... --allowed-root R [--deliverable T] [--allow-discovery], operator discover run <exp, and python scripts\hive_admission.py initadmitrevokerollback. The runbook is docs/OPERATOR_RUNBOOK.md in the package. For headless checks, add --no-browser; the plain launcher opens a browser that holds the session token. Limits - Trusted local scope only. Nothing here is production-approved. - Admission trust is one Windows user. The signer public key is committed in configs/admission_signers. The private key sits in %USERPROFILE%\.hive-admission, outside the repository and store, so anything running as that user can read it. Candidate code (in a container with no network or files) and the store writer cannot mint admissions. A forged or unsigned event fails the whole capability chain closed. Receipts are integrity-hashed, not signed; admission re-runs the evaluator instead of trusting them. - Rollback is proven only by a test fixture. There is one real admitted version, so a live rollback refuses with UNAVAILABLE. - One workload, one model. The step was found once, on one real workload, by one local model. - Known gaps: the wall-time budget is checked before each step, not during one. The planner explores only the first match for single-input capabilities. Snapshot intermediates cannot be downloaded. The capability id inventory-diff is hardcoded in admission. - Behaviour change: an unqualified requested model is now refused, even in shadow mode. - Tested on one Windows 11 host with Docker Desktop and a 16 GB GPU (peak about 15.3 GB with the model loaded). Tests - Full suite on the final code 033089b: 1114 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed (1 h 10 min, Docker up). - An earlier full run on 965aedd had 22 failures. 21 came from evaluator folders sharing bare module names, fixed in 033089b without changing any pinned evaluator file. The 22nd was a ledger-lock timeout that also failed on the old baseline under load, and it passed on the final run. - Clean launch: the package extracted to a fresh folder imported OK, reported readiness at 033089b, and contains no keys, private cases or SQLite stores. Evidence Checkpoint report · gate summaries C1+C2, C3, C4, C5, C6. Receipts are listed as ids and hashes only. C3 candidate e5765a1c...e88c, evaluator receipt 92c1bdf8...86d7, C4 admission statement 5883be35...89e6, signer SHA256:Yk7d2kF/AEKCd7Fi+CZJa0XxBOnkOZ10aX8khS9gkVc.
